title: Hall and Yard
text:
1. The Harborwick site consists of a single-storey warehouse hall of 6,000 m² with 10 m clear internal height, plus a small office annex attached to the hall. The hall contains all operational zones A–F. No storage or operational activity takes place outside the hall except for vehicle movement and dock operations.

2. The site is enclosed by perimeter fencing. The fenced yard area is 3,500 m² and provides circulation for goods vehicles, access to all dock doors, and the marked driver waiting area. Drivers do not enter the hall.

3. The hall is served by eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, all located on the yard side of the building. Each dock door is equipped with its own dock leveller. The doors are dedicated by direction of flow.

4. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only. No inbound unloading is permitted at an outbound door and no outbound loading is permitted at an inbound door. Door allocation and time slots are assigned by the dispatcher.

5. Internal circulation is based on a defined aisle network. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide the primary routes for materials handling equipment between zones and to and from the docks.

6. Rack storage aisles in the bulk storage area are 3.0 m wide. These aisles are for pallet put-away and retrieval only and are not used as through-routes for general transport unless required for the task.

7. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated from vehicle routes by fixed yellow barriers. All separated walkways are 1.2 m wide and are the only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas.

8. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, the meeting points are marked as pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramp areas. These areas are clearly signed and marked on the floor.

9. Speed limits apply to all powered equipment, including counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks, and to all visiting vehicles in the yard. The limits are enforced in all shifts without exception.

10. Inside the building the maximum speed is 10 km/h. In the yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. In all marked pedestrian zones, at all pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h.

11. The yard layout provides sufficient turning and queuing space for curtain-side trailers and delivery vans to access their assigned doors without obstructing other doors. Vehicles waiting for a slot wait only in the marked waiting area in the yard.

12. Any change to hall layout, yard markings, barriers, dock designation or speed limits requires approval by the warehouse manager before implementation. Temporary obstructions to aisles, walkways or dock approaches are not permitted unless controlled by the shift supervisor.

title: Floor Zones A–F
text:
1. The hall floor is divided into six permanently marked zones, Zone A to Zone F. The zones cover the entire 6,000 m² hall: Zone A 800 m², Zone B 2,200 m², Zone C 1,200 m², Zone D 900 m², Zone E 300 m² and Zone F 600 m². Boundaries are painted on the floor, signed overhead and shown on the site plan at each entrance. All tasks, scanner instructions and shift briefings use zone letters.

2. Zone A is receiving. It lies immediately inside inbound doors 1 to 4 and contains the unloading lanes, inspection benches and document-check area. All inbound goods are received, counted and inspected in Zone A. No pallet moves beyond Zone A until paperwork has been checked and the delivery accepted.

3. Zone B is bulk storage. It occupies 2,200 m² and provides 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay pallet racking. Each rack bay in Zone B is limited to 2,700 kg. Where block stacking is used outside racking, stacks in Zone B are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high.

4. Zone C is picking. It occupies 1,200 m² and contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone C holds no bulk reserve stock; all pick faces in Zone C are fed by replenishment from Zone B before each picking shift.

5. Zone D is dispatch. It occupies 900 m² directly in front of outbound doors 5 to 8 and is used solely for outbound staging. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets are placed in Zone D, staged by outbound door and load.

6. Zone E is the cold zone. It is a physically segregated chilled area of 300 m² held between +2 °C and +8 °C. Zone E is fitted with continuous temperature monitoring and audible alarms, supplemented by manual temperature verification in Zone E each shift.

7. Zone F is services and control. It occupies 600 m² and contains value-added packing, the quarantine area and the returns inspection area. Goods in quarantine in Zone F remain physically separated and clearly identified until formally released or written off.

8. Inside Zone F is the separate ventilated hazmat cage. The cage occupies 60 m² within Zone F. All hazardous materials on site are stored only inside this cage in Zone F and never in any other zone. Total quantity in the hazmat cage in Zone F never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time.

9. Movement between zones follows the fixed flow: inbound goods enter Zone A, then booked goods are put away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F; replenishment moves pallets from Zone B to Zone C; picked and packed pallets move from Zone C to Zone D for dispatch. Returns and damaged goods move to Zone F.

10. Storage outside marked zones is not permitted. Pallets, cages, packing materials and waste handling equipment are stored only within their allocated zone. Aisles, pedestrian walkways and dock approaches in all zones are kept clear at all times.

11. Zone designations are fixed. Any change to zone boundaries, zone use or the location of the hazmat cage within Zone F requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan and WMS locations before use.

title: Docks and Yard Access
text:
1. Access to the yard is through the fenced perimeter gates. The yard of 3,500 m² provides one-way circulation for goods vehicles to and from the eight dock doors. Only authorised vehicles, employees and escorted visitors are permitted inside the fence.

2. All eight dock doors are located on the yard side of the hall at 1.2 m dock height. Each door is equipped with its own dock leveller. A leveller is operated only by trained warehouse staff and only for the vehicle currently assigned to that door.

3. Doors are dedicated by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading. No door is used for the opposite flow for any reason.

4. Every carrier is assigned a door and a time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. No vehicle approaches a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

5. On arrival, drivers report to the gate or to the dispatcher and then move only to their assigned door at the assigned time. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall.

6. The marked waiting area is the only permitted waiting place for drivers and for vehicles queuing for a slot. Vehicles waiting for a slot wait only there and do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes.

7. No unloading or loading begins until the vehicle is correctly positioned at the assigned door, the engine is stopped, the parking brake is applied and the dock leveller is safely deployed by warehouse staff. Dock doors remain closed when not in active use.

8. Inbound operators and forklift operators work inside the hall and on the dock levellers in Zone A at doors 1 to 4 to unload. Dispatch and warehouse staff work in Zone D at doors 5 to 8 to load. Drivers do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors.

9. Pedestrian access to the dock area is only via the physically separated 1.2 m wide walkways with fixed yellow barriers. Where walkways meet vehicle lanes, the crossings are marked and signed. No pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at a dock or crosses a dock ramp unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

10. Yard traffic uses the marked lanes to reach the assigned door and to exit without reversing across other doors where possible. Sufficient turning and queuing space is maintained so that a vehicle at one door does not block access to any other door.

11. Speed limits are enforced for all powered equipment and all visiting vehicles. The maximum speed in the yard is 15 km/h. Inside the building the maximum is 10 km/h. At all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps, in the yard and in the hall, the maximum is 5 km/h.

12. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m width provide the link between the docks and Zones A to F. Rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are not used as through-routes to the docks except for put-away and retrieval tasks.

13. Any obstruction to a dock approach, yard lane, walkway or crossing is not permitted. Waste, pallets, stretch wrap materials and handling equipment are not staged in the yard or across dock approaches. The shift supervisor controls any temporary closure of a door or yard lane and informs the dispatcher immediately.

14. Changes to door designations, time-slot arrangements, waiting area location, yard markings, barriers or leveller operating arrangements require prior approval by the warehouse manager before implementation.

title: Roles on Site
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. employs 38 to 40 people on site in defined roles. Every person is assigned to one role with fixed duties by zone and procedure. No task is carried out outside its assigned role and zone.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs. The manager is the only person who authorises new forklift operators and overtime and signs off stocktake results and write-offs above 500 EUR.

3. Two shift supervisors provide cover for the two-shift pattern, one supervisor in charge of the floor on each shift. A shift supervisor runs the floor staff, controls the shift workflow between Zones A to F, and leads incident response on that shift.

4. Eight forklift operators operate materials handling equipment. They drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, and electric pallet jacks for general pallet moves. They work to WMS tasks for put-away, replenishment and loading.

5. Six inbound operators work in Zone A at inbound doors 1 to 4. They check delivery paperwork before unloading, unload vehicles, count and inspect goods, and present accepted goods for system booking. No goods move beyond Zone A until they have completed these checks.

6. Ten pickers work in Zone C. They pick customer orders against scanner-directed tasks from ground-level pick faces and flow racks, scan-verify each pick, and move picked goods for packing and transfer to Zone D.

7. Two stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. They plan and execute cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, carry out second counts and recounts, investigate discrepancies, and prepare adjustments for approval. They do not post adjustments without a second count.

8. Four returns and packing staff work in Zone F. They inspect all returned goods, record condition, and propose disposition as restock, rework or scrap. They also carry out value-added packing tasks in Zone F as directed.

9. One maintenance technician maintains all materials handling equipment, racking and dock equipment including dock levellers. The technician carries out planned checks, repairs and racking inspections and logs every repair and inspection in the maintenance record.

10. Two dispatchers control outbound flow and transport. They book carriers, assign each carrier a door and time slot, manage the yard waiting area, and release outbound loads from Zone D at doors 5 to 8. No vehicle is loaded without dispatcher release.

11. Two floaters provide cover for absence across inbound, picking, packing and dispatch. When covering a role, a floater works only within the duties of that role and under the shift supervisor's direction.

12. Forklift and reach truck operation is restricted to authorised forklift operators only. Authorisation is granted personally by the warehouse manager after licence and training verification. No other role operates those trucks for any reason.

13. All roles operate within procedures PR-01 to PR-15. Shift supervisors direct task allocation on the floor, but role boundaries remain: inbound operators do not pick, pickers do not put away to high bays, and stock controllers do not handle returns disposition except through the count process.

14. Every person on the warehouse floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear as required for their zone. Each role is responsible for keeping its work area, aisles and dock approaches clear and for reporting hazards to the shift supervisor immediately.

title: Approvals and Accountability
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site, for operations, safety and inventory accuracy. No operational activity takes place outside the manager's responsibility, and no approval exceeds the manager's authority.

2. The warehouse manager provides all final sign-offs for the site. This includes the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results, and any adjustment arising from the annual stocktake, before the system is updated.

3. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift and reach truck operators. Authorisation is personal, in writing, after verification of licence and training, and no person operates a counterbalance forklift rated at 2.5 t or reach truck rated at 1.6 t without it.

4. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime. The decision covers Saturday morning overtime in peak season and any extension beyond 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, and is recorded by the shift supervisor.

5. The shift supervisor is in charge of the floor on each shift and is accountable for staff direction, workflow between Zones A to F and immediate incident response. One shift supervisor is present on every shift.

6. Write-offs for damaged goods are approved by value threshold. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR after same-day quarantine in Zone F. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR.

7. Returns staff in Zone F inspect every return received within 14 days of delivery and propose disposition as restock, rework or scrap. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of all inspected returns before any goods move from Zone F.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising on that shift, including safety events, damage to racking or equipment, temperature alarms in Zone E and spills in the hazmat cage in Zone F, and initiates corrective action.

9. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. The dispatcher books transport and assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot: doors 1 to 4 for inbound, doors 5 to 8 for outbound. No assignment is changed on the floor without dispatcher confirmation.

10. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day and prepare all inventory adjustments. No adjustment is posted without a second count. Adjustments following daily cycle counts are approved by the shift supervisor; adjustments following the annual stocktake are approved only by the warehouse manager.

11. The maintenance technician is accountable for logging every repair and inspection of materials handling equipment, racking and dock levellers. Any repair affecting load capacity, safety barriers, leveller operation or rack bay limits of 2,700 kg is reported to the shift supervisor and approved by the warehouse manager before return to service.

12. Changes to fixed site standards require prior approval by the warehouse manager. This includes any change to hall or yard layout, zone boundaries or zone use, the location of the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F, the 4,000 kg hazmat limit, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, pedestrian walkway provision of 1.2 m, barriers, dock designations, time-slot arrangements and speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

13. Approvals are not delegable except where this manual expressly states a threshold. Where a threshold is stated, the decision is taken only by the named role at paragraph 2 to 10, and the approval is recorded with name, date and value or quantity.

14. If doubt arises on authority, the shift supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager before action. The brief from the owner prevails over any conflicting instruction in this manual.

title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
text:
1. One shift supervisor is in charge of the floor on every shift. The site operates Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only when approved by the warehouse manager. No shift operates without its supervisor present.

2. The shift supervisor directs all floor staff on that shift across Zones A to F. This includes inbound operators in Zone A, forklift operators on put-away, replenishment and loading, pickers in Zone C, returns and packing staff in Zone F, floaters covering absence, and the maintenance technician for immediate tasks.

3. Task allocation, work sequencing between zones and the order of work at the docks are controlled by the shift supervisor. Work is issued through WMS tasks and verbal briefing, but the supervisor retains authority to reprioritise to maintain flow and safety.

4. The shift supervisor is the incident lead on that shift. All injuries, damage to racking or equipment, spills, temperature alarms in Zone E, and any departure from procedure is reported immediately to the supervisor, who secures the area and initiates response in accordance with PR-09, PR-13 and PR-14.

5. The shift supervisor enforces standards on the floor, including high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for everyone on the floor, seat-belt use on forklifts, speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and the use of physically separated 1.2 m walkways.

6. The shift supervisor controls any temporary obstruction, closure of an aisle, walkway or dock approach, and any short-notice change to floor activity. The dispatcher is informed immediately of any door or lane that is not available for use.

7. The shift supervisor approves on the floor within fixed thresholds: damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR after quarantine in Zone F, the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap in Zone F, and reviews every incident report arising on that shift before close.

8. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport and assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot. Doors 1 to 4 are inbound only and doors 5 to 8 are outbound only, with no opposite-flow use.

9. No vehicle approaches a door, is unloaded in Zone A or is loaded in Zone D without a confirmed door and time-slot assignment from the dispatcher. Door changes, time-slot changes and re-bookings are made only by the dispatcher.

10. On arrival, drivers report as directed and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to the door only at the assigned time.

11. Dock levellers at all eight 1.2 m doors are operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently assigned to that door. Unloading and loading begin only when the vehicle is correctly positioned, engine stopped, parking brake applied and leveller safely deployed.

12. The dispatcher releases every outbound load from Zone D. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets staged by door and load in Zone D are loaded, and no loading proceeds without dispatcher release.

13. The shift supervisor and the dispatcher coordinate continuously during the shift. The dispatcher controls which door and when, the supervisor controls how the floor prepares, stages and executes the work safely in Zones A to D. If a conflict arises between floor readiness and the dock plan, the dispatcher decides the door plan and the supervisor decides the safe method of work.

14. End-of-shift handover between supervisors includes dock status, waiting vehicles, incomplete loads, quarantined goods, open incidents and equipment defects, in accordance with PR-15. The outgoing supervisor remains accountable until handover to the incoming supervisor is complete.

title: Working Hours
text:
1. The site operates on a two-shift pattern, Monday to Friday. The morning shift runs 06:00 to 14:00. The afternoon shift runs 14:00 to 22:00. All warehouse activity in Zones A to F and all dock activity at doors 1 to 8 takes place within these hours.

2. No shift operates without its shift supervisor present and in charge of the floor. One shift supervisor is assigned to each shift and remains on site and contactable for the full 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 period, including during breaks.

3. Standard working hours apply to all roles on site: warehouse manager, shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, maintenance technician, dispatchers and floaters. Start and finish times are as rostered within the two-shift pattern.

4. The morning and afternoon shifts provide continuous cover Monday to Friday. Handover between shifts takes place at 14:00, with the outgoing supervisor briefing the incoming supervisor on dock status, work in progress and any incidents before leaving the floor, in accordance with PR-15.

5. There is no routine weekend working. Saturday and Sunday are non-working days, except for Saturday morning overtime in peak season as described below. No picking, put-away, receiving or dispatch is scheduled outside Monday to Friday without an approved overtime arrangement.

6. In peak season the site may add Saturday morning overtime to meet outbound and inbound demand. Saturday overtime is limited to the morning period only. No Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday working is scheduled.

7. Overtime is approved only by the warehouse manager. No other role authorises overtime, extends a shift beyond 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00, or calls staff in for Saturday morning work. Approval is personal and given in advance where possible.

8. Every overtime approval is recorded, including date, shift or Saturday period, roles required and reason. The shift supervisor records the approval and the staff rostered, and ensures only approved staff attend for the approved period.

9. Where overtime is approved, task allocation and safe staffing levels remain under the shift supervisor's control. The supervisor confirms sufficient cover for the planned work across Zones A to F, for dock operations at the assigned doors, and for supervision, first-aid and emergency response.

10. Staff are not permitted to remain on the warehouse floor or in the yard outside their rostered shift or approved overtime period unless directed by the shift supervisor for a specific operational or safety reason. Drivers and visitors are not permitted outside assigned door times for any reason.

11. Any change to the standard pattern of 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, or to the arrangements for Saturday morning overtime, requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before publication to staff or to carriers. Temporary obstructions or early closures are controlled by the shift supervisor and notified to the dispatcher immediately.

12. Attendance, absence and lateness during working hours are managed by the shift supervisor on each shift. The supervisor deploys the two floaters to cover absence within the approved shift pattern. If cover cannot be maintained safely, the supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager before reducing dock activity or outbound releases.

title: End-of-Shift Handover
text:
1. Handover between supervisors is carried out under PR-15 at every shift change. The standard handover takes place at 14:00 between the morning supervisor going off duty and the afternoon supervisor coming on duty. At the end of the afternoon shift at 22:00, the supervisor closes the site under PR-15 and records the overnight status for the next morning shift at 06:00.

2. Handover is conducted face to face on the warehouse floor and takes precedence over other tasks. Both supervisors are present for the full exchange. The outgoing supervisor remains accountable for the floor in all zones A to F and for dock doors 1 to 8 until handover is complete and acknowledged.

3. Where Saturday morning overtime has been approved in advance by the warehouse manager, the designated supervisor carries out opening handover at 06:00 and closing handover at the end of the approved morning period using the same PR-15 process. No handover takes place outside approved working hours.

4. The outgoing supervisor provides a status report by zone. This includes goods still in Zone A awaiting document check, count or inspection; bulk positions in Zone B affected by damage or reservation; pick faces in Zone C awaiting replenishment; staged loads in Zone D by outbound door 5 to 8; manual temperature verification for Zone E; and quarantine, returns or hazmat cage activity in Zone F.

5. Dock status is handed over explicitly. The report covers which doors are occupied, which carriers have a confirmed door and time-slot assignment from the dispatcher, vehicles in the marked waiting area, incomplete unloads at doors 1 to 4, and incomplete or released but not yet loaded outbound loads at doors 5 to 8.

6. Work in progress in the WMS is handed over, including open put-away, replenishment, picking, packing and dispatch tasks, the location of the 20 handheld scanners, and any scanner or system faults that affect task issue.

7. Safety and incident status is handed over. The outgoing supervisor reports all injuries, near misses, racking or equipment damage, temperature alarms in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, and spills or quantity changes in the 60 m² hazmat cage in Zone F, with reference to incident reports reviewed on that shift under PR-09, PR-13 and PR-14.

8. Equipment and site defects are handed over. This includes defects on the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, dock levellers, stretch wrappers and baler, any documented daily check failures, rack bay damage in Zone B, and any temporary closure of an aisle, walkway or dock approach.

9. No adjustment is handed over as complete unless supported by a second count. Cycle count results, recounts required and pending approvals for write-offs up to 500 EUR by the shift supervisor or above 500 EUR by the warehouse manager are identified for the incoming supervisor.

10. The incoming supervisor confirms understanding, checks the physical status of Zones A to F and the dock doors where needed, and accepts responsibility for staff direction, speed-limit and PPE enforcement, supervision of pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m, and emergency response for the next shift.

11. Handover is recorded under PR-15 in the shift handover log. The record includes date, shift times 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00, names of both supervisors, dock and zone status, open incidents and equipment defects, and the time responsibility transfers. Both supervisors sign the record.

12. If the incoming supervisor is delayed, the outgoing supervisor retains charge of the floor and no staff operate unsupervised. The delay is notified to the warehouse manager and work is held at a safe point until handover is completed.

title: Arrival and Door Assignment
text:
ops.ch04.s1 Arrival and Door Assignment

1. All inbound deliveries arrive only at doors 1, 2, 3 and 4. No inbound vehicle is received at doors 5 to 8 for any reason. Inbound receiving in Zone A operates only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager.

2. Every inbound carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for doors 1 to 4. No assignment is made or changed on the floor without dispatcher confirmation.

3. Carriers are instructed to report arrival to the gate or to the dispatcher and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall and never approach a door until called forward at the assigned time.

4. Vehicles arriving early or late for their slot wait only in the marked waiting area and do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes. The dispatcher reschedules late or unscheduled arrivals to the next available inbound slot and informs the shift supervisor.

5. No vehicle moves to a door until the dispatcher has confirmed the door is free and the shift supervisor has confirmed Zone A has capacity to receive. The yard speed limit of 15 km/h and the 5 km/h limit at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all movements to the door.

6. On being called forward, the driver positions the vehicle squarely at the assigned door, stops the engine, applies the parking brake and hands over delivery documents from the cab or waiting area. The dock door remains closed until staff are ready.

7. Unloading does not begin until the vehicle is correctly positioned and secured and the dock leveller for that door has been safely deployed by trained warehouse staff. Levellers are operated only for the vehicle currently assigned to that door.

8. Under PR-01, document check takes place in Zone A before anything is unloaded. Six inbound operators work in Zone A and check paperwork at the document-check area inside doors 1 to 4. No pallet is removed from the vehicle until the check is complete.

9. The check verifies carrier identity, booking reference, door and time-slot assignment, purchase order or inbound reference, supplier, number of pallets and product description against the expected inbound record. Any seal number is recorded where applicable.

10. If documents are missing, do not match the booking, or refer to unscheduled goods, unloading is held. The inbound operator immediately escalates to the shift supervisor and the dispatcher. No goods move past Zone A and no booking is made in the system until the discrepancy is resolved.

11. Where the document check identifies overage that would breach site limits, including the hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F or the pallet weight limit of 900 kg, the delivery is held in the vehicle or in Zone A in its holding location and the shift supervisor decides acceptance, partial acceptance or refusal with dispatcher support.

12. Accepted deliveries are confirmed as accepted on the paperwork with date, time, door number, name of the checker and signature. Only after this confirmation do inbound operators begin unloading in accordance with PR-01. The dispatcher and shift supervisor update the door board to show the door as occupied for unloading.

13. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area during unloading, do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and do not enter Zone A. Any temporary closure of an inbound door or waiting area is controlled by the shift supervisor and notified to the dispatcher immediately.

title: Unloading, Count and Inspection
text:
1. Unloading in Zone A begins only after the document check in paragraph ops.ch04.s1 is complete, accepted and signed off. No pallet is removed from the vehicle before that point, and no goods leave Zone A until count and inspection are finished.

2. The inbound operators working at doors 1 to 4 carry out unloading. Forklift operators assist with palletised loads using the 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts, 1.6 t reach trucks where needed and electric or hand pallet jacks. Only authorised operators drive counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks.

3. Unloading is done on the dock leveller for the assigned door, operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently at that door. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area in the yard and do not enter Zone A or operate any equipment.

4. Speed limits apply throughout unloading and movement within Zone A: 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

5. Every pallet is checked against the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load. Any pallet indicating overweight, unstable stacking, visible collapse or unsafe wrapping is held in Zone A and reported immediately to the shift supervisor. It does not proceed to put-away.

6. Count takes place in Zone A immediately after unloading. Inbound operators count pallets and units by purchase order or inbound reference and compare the count to the checked delivery documents and booking reference. The count result is recorded with date, time, door and name of checker.

7. Inspection is carried out at the same time in Zone A. Each pallet and its goods are visually inspected for damage, wet packaging, leakage, seal integrity, labelling accuracy and, where applicable, temperature condition and expiry date. For chilled goods for Zone E, condition and temperature are noted for manual verification.

8. Goods arriving for hazardous storage are identified during inspection. They are held separately in Zone A pending check of quantity against the 4,000 kg limit for the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. No hazmat quantity above that limit is accepted into Zone A.

9. Where count or inspection identifies shortage, overage or damage, the inbound operator immediately escalates to the shift supervisor. Shortages and overages are noted on the delivery paperwork and in the WMS receiving record. Overage that would breach site limits is held in Zone A for supervisor decision on partial acceptance or refusal.

10. Damaged goods are not counted as available stock. They are segregated, clearly identified and moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day they are found, in accordance with PR-09. The quantity, nature of damage and pallet reference are recorded on the quarantine record for write-off approval by value threshold.

11. No goods are booked into the system until inspection is complete. Under PR-01, only inspected goods in Zone A are eligible for system booking, and only booked goods are released for physical put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Uninspected goods remain in Zone A and are not moved to bulk storage, cold zone or hazmat cage.

12. On completion of count and inspection, inbound operators confirm the accepted quantity as counted and inspected on the paperwork, with signatures for unload, count and inspection. The shift supervisor is notified of any exceptions, quarantine moves and any inbound that cannot proceed to booking.

13. Unloading equipment is cleared from Zone A and returned to its designated area. Zone A lanes, inspection benches and dock approaches are left clear for the next time slot, and the dispatcher updates dock status for doors 1 to 4.

title: System Booking and Release to Put-Away
text:
1. No pallet moves out of Zone A to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F until it is booked in the WMS and released for put-away. Physical movement past Zone A and system booking are the same gate: inspected goods in Zone A are booked first, then and only then are they moved.

2. Booking is carried out in Zone A immediately after count and inspection under PR-01. Inbound operators use the handheld WMS scanners to create the inbound receipt against the checked booking reference, purchase order and supplier, recording SKU, quantity, pallet identity, expiry date where applicable, and pallet weight for the 1,000 kg limit.

3. A pallet that fails the weight, stability or packaging check is not booked as available stock. It remains in its holding location in Zone A for shift supervisor decision and, if accepted after rework, is re-counted and re-inspected before booking.

4. On successful booking the WMS generates a pallet licence plate and put-away task with a directed storage location. No hand-written location, verbal instruction or pre-printed label replaces the system task. Pallets without a WMS pallet label are not released.

5. Release to put-away requires three confirmations in Zone A: documents checked and signed off, count and inspection recorded, and WMS booking completed with pallet label applied and scannable. The checker’s name, date, time and door 1 to 4 are recorded on the receipt.

6. Forklift operators execute put-away only against a released WMS task on a handheld scanner. They scan the pallet licence plate in Zone A and the destination location in Zone B, Zone E or Zone F to close the move. A pallet scanned in Zone A that is not released is rejected by the system.

7. Put-away to Zone B is directed only to a vacant pallet position within the 2,400 positions and within the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg, or to block stacking at 3 pallets high and 4.0 m where designated. The WMS does not direct put-away to an occupied, damaged or reserved bay.

8. Put-away to Zone E is released only after temperature condition has been noted in Zone A and the pallet is booked with cold-chain status. Pallets for Zone E are not staged in ambient zones and are moved directly to their directed chilled location between +2 °C and +8 °C.

9. Put-away to the hazmat cage in Zone F is released only after the quantity is checked against the cage limit of 4,000 kg in the 60 m² ventilated cage. The WMS blocks release if the receipt would exceed the limit; excess remains in Zone A for supervisor decision on partial acceptance or refusal.

10. Damaged goods segregated in Zone A are not booked as available. Where moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 they are booked to quarantine status only, clearly identified and physically separated, pending write-off approval by value threshold.

11. Any booking discrepancy, label failure, scanner fault or location block is reported immediately to the shift supervisor in Zone A. The pallet remains in Zone A and is not moved to Zone B, E or F until the error is corrected and a new system task is issued.

12. Zone A lanes are cleared only after all pallets for the delivery are booked and released or formally held as exceptions. The dispatcher is then notified that doors 1 to 4 are free for the next assigned slot, and the shift supervisor confirms the gate is closed before the next inbound is called forward.

title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
text:
1. Zone B is bulk storage and occupies 2,200 m² of the hall. It provides high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions forming the bulk reserve for the site. Zone B holds only booked and system-directed stock put away from Zone A under PR-02.

2. Every pallet stored in Zone B, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This 1,000 kg limit is the basis for all rack and stacking capacities in Zone B and is checked at booking in Zone A before any put-away task is released.

3. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total. The WMS directs put-away only to a vacant position within this bay limit and blocks any move that would exceed 2,700 kg in the bay. No additional pallet is placed in a bay once the limit is reached.

4. Where block stacking is used outside racking in Zone B, stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high, including the pallet. No block stack exceeds either limit, and no block stacking takes place in rack aisles, against rack uprights, or across main transport aisles.

5. Put-away to Zone B is executed only against a released WMS task on a handheld scanner. The forklift operator scans the pallet licence plate in Zone A and the destination location in Zone B to close the move. Hand-written locations, verbal instructions or unlabelled pallets are not permitted in Zone B.

6. High-bay put-away and retrieval in Zone B are carried out only by authorised forklift operators. The 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are used for high-bay work; the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and electric pallet jacks are used for general pallet moves to and from Zone B as directed by task.

7. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide and are for put-away and retrieval only. They are not used as through-routes for general transport. Main transport aisles linking Zone B to Zones A, C and D are 4.0 m wide and provide the primary routes for materials handling equipment.

8. Hazardous materials are never stored in Zone B. All hazmat on site is stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F, subject to the cage limit of 4,000 kg. Chilled goods for Zone E and quarantined goods for Zone F are not stored in Zone B.

9. Only stable, undamaged and correctly wrapped pallets are stored in Zone B, with the load within the pallet footprint and not overhanging uprights or beams. A pallet found damaged, leaning, leaking or unstable in Zone B is not re-stored. It is made safe, segregated and moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day it is found under PR-09, and the bay is left empty until cleared.

10. Racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month by the maintenance technician, with every repair and inspection logged. Any damage to uprights, beams, bracing or floor fixings, or any defect affecting the 2,700 kg bay limit, is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the bay is blocked in the WMS until approved for return to service by the warehouse manager.

11. Pedestrian walkways through and around Zone B are physically separated by fixed yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide. Pedestrians use only these walkways, and where they meet vehicle routes the crossings are marked and signed. Forklift seat belts, high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone B.

12. Speed limits in Zone B are enforced on all powered equipment: 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Aisles, walkways, rack ends and fire exits in Zone B are kept clear at all times, with no staging of packing materials, waste or handling equipment.

13. Storage outside marked rack positions and designated block-stack areas in Zone B is not permitted. Any change to rack layout, bay capacity, block-stack areas, aisle widths or barriers in Zone B requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan and WMS locations before use.

title: Cold Zone E
text:
1. Zone E is the chilled storage zone and occupies 300 m² within the hall. It is a physically segregated, insulated enclosure with self-closing doors, held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C. Zone E stores only booked goods requiring chilled conditions under PR-12.

2. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +8 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced without investigation.

3. In addition to continuous monitoring, a manual temperature verification is carried out in Zone E on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. The check is performed by the designated operator, recorded with date, time, measured temperature, name and signature, and countersigned by the shift supervisor. The log is retained in Zone E.

4. Put-away to Zone E is released only from Zone A after count, inspection and cold-chain status have been noted and the pallet has been booked in the WMS. Pallets for Zone E are moved directly to their directed chilled location and are not staged in ambient zones A, B, C or D.

5. Every pallet stored in Zone E, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. The WMS directs put-away only to a vacant, serviceable chilled location. No pallet is placed outside marked chilled positions, in doorways, against evaporators or across aisles.

6. Goods in Zone E remain on pallets, stable, wrapped and within the pallet footprint. Where racking is used, pallet positions are clearly marked; where floor locations are used, spacing preserves airflow and access for stock checks. Doors to Zone E remain closed except during active put-away, replenishment or picking.

7. No hazardous materials are stored in Zone E. All hazmat on site is stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F, subject to the 4,000 kg limit. No quarantine stock is held in Zone E; damaged or suspect chilled goods are segregated in place and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

8. Only authorised forklift operators and inbound operators acting on a WMS task enter Zone E for put-away. Exposure time is minimised: equipment and personnel enter only to complete the directed task and then exit, closing the doors. Electric pallet jacks used in Zone E are rated for chilled operation.

9. Speed limits apply inside Zone E as inside the building: 10 km/h maximum, and 5 km/h at the marked pedestrian zone and crossing at the Zone E doors. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways where provided. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone E; additional insulated clothing is worn as required.

10. Any temperature excursion, alarm, door fault, icing, condensation, leakage or evidence of cold-chain breach is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The supervisor secures the stock in place, prevents despatch of affected pallets and initiates response under PR-12 and PR-09. Affected pallets are not picked or replenished to Zone C until cleared.

11. Cycle counts in Zone E are carried out on the rotating schedule and require short, planned door openings only. Stock controllers coordinate counts with the shift supervisor to limit door open time. No adjustment for Zone E is posted without a second count, in accordance with PR-08.

12. The maintenance technician maintains the refrigeration plant, doors, monitoring and alarm system for Zone E and logs every repair and inspection. Any defect affecting temperature holding, monitoring or alarms is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the warehouse manager, and Zone E is not used for new put-away until the system is verified within +2 °C to +8 °C.

title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
text:
1. Zone F occupies 600 m² and contains value-added packing, the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the separate ventilated hazmat cage. Zone F holds only goods booked to quarantine, returns or hazmat status under PR-09 and PR-13, or goods directed to packing tasks.

2. The hazmat cage occupies 60 m² within Zone F. It is a physically separated, signposted and locked enclosure with forced ventilation, spill containment and restricted access. All hazardous materials on site are stored only inside this 60 m² cage and never in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E.

3. Total quantity in the hazmat cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time. With the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load, this means at most 4 full-weight pallets in the cage at any time. The WMS blocks any receipt or put-away that would exceed 4,000 kg, and excess remains in Zone A for supervisor decision.

4. Put-away to the hazmat cage is released only from Zone A after document check, count and inspection under PR-01 and PR-13. Quantity is checked against the 4,000 kg cage limit before booking, and forklift operators move pallets only against a released WMS task to a directed vacant location in the 60 m² cage.

5. Pallets stored in the cage are stable, intact, correctly labelled and within the pallet footprint. Incompatible hazard classes are segregated inside the cage as marked. No pallet is stored outside marked hazmat positions, against ventilation openings, doors or spill bunds.

6. Access to the 60 m² hazmat cage is restricted to authorised forklift operators and the shift supervisor. The cage remains locked when not in active put-away or retrieval. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, with additional PPE as specified on the safety data sheet.

7. The 4,000 kg limit is displayed at the cage entrance and on the Zone F site plan. Any proposal to change the cage location within Zone F, the cage size of 60 m² or the 4,000 kg limit requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and update to WMS locations before use.

8. Any damaged, leaking or suspect hazmat pallet in any zone is made safe, segregated in place and moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day it is found under PR-09. Spills in the cage are dealt with immediately under PR-13 using the spill kit at Zone F, and the shift supervisor is notified at once.

9. The quarantine area in Zone F is a physically separated, barriered and clearly signed area for damaged goods and for inspected returns pending disposition. Goods in quarantine remain clearly identified by quarantine labels and pallet status and are not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

10. Damaged goods found during receiving, storage in Zone B, cold storage in Zone E or picking in Zone C are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day, booked to quarantine status in the WMS and recorded with date, SKU, quantity, location and reason. Only quarantined stock is considered for write-off.

11. Returns inspected in Zone F that are assessed as not suitable for immediate restock are held in quarantine pending final disposition. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap, and the shift supervisor approves the final disposition before any move from Zone F.

12. No goods leave quarantine without approval. Write-offs for damaged goods are approved by value threshold: up to and including 500 EUR by the shift supervisor, above 500 EUR by the warehouse manager. The approval is recorded with name, date and value.

13. Speed limits in Zone F are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and the Zone F access. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers. Aisles, cage approaches and quarantine lanes are kept clear at all times.

14. The maintenance technician inspects the hazmat cage, ventilation, containment, racking and signage and logs every inspection and repair. Any defect affecting ventilation, containment, cage security or the availability of quarantine locations is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the cage is not used for new put-away until cleared by the warehouse manager.

title: Replenishment of Pick Faces
text:
1. Replenishment of pick faces in Zone C is carried out under PR-03 before each picking shift. The purpose is to fill ground-level pick faces and flow racks in Zone C from bulk reserve in Zone B so that pickers work only from fully stocked faces during 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00.

2. Zone C holds no bulk reserve. Zone C occupies 1,200 m² and contains only pick faces and flow racks fed by replenishment from Zone B. No pallet remains in Zone C as reserve stock and no put-away from Zone A goes directly to Zone C.

3. Replenishment tasks are system-directed. The WMS generates replenishment tasks before the shift based on current pick-face levels, open customer orders and available booked stock in Zone B. No hand-written location, verbal instruction or unlabelled pallet is used for replenishment.

4. Only forklift operators execute replenishment moves, using WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners. High-bay retrieval in Zone B is carried out with the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t; general moves of full pallets to Zone C use the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and electric pallet jacks as directed. Only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive those trucks.

5. The shift supervisor controls sequencing of replenishment on the floor. Replenishment is sequenced by priority of the next wave of picks, flow-rack lanes needing fill and any stock events in Zone B. The supervisor confirms that Zone B aisles, main transport aisles of 4.0 m and Zone C feed lanes are clear before work begins.

6. Every pallet moved for replenishment, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. The pallet is already booked and within the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg in Zone B. A pallet found overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking or with damaged wrapping is not moved to Zone C. It is segregated and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and the location is left empty.

7. The operator scans the source location in Zone B and the pallet licence plate to confirm correct stock, then scans the destination pick face or flow-rack lane in Zone C to close the task. If the scan does not match the directed locations, the system rejects the move and the operator reports the discrepancy to the shift supervisor before any further move.

8. Pallets for replenishment are taken only from verified bulk positions in Zone B, including the 2,400 high-bay positions and designated block-stack areas at 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high. A damaged, reserved or blocked bay in Zone B is not used for replenishment until cleared by the warehouse manager.

9. Flow racks in Zone C are fed from the rear replenishment side and picked from the front pick side. Ground-level faces are replenished by placing the full pallet in the marked face position with labels facing the aisle and the load fully within the pallet footprint. No pallet overhangs racking or blocks the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

10. Replenishment is complete before picking against scanner tasks begins on that shift. The shift supervisor checks WMS completion of PR-03 tasks, verifies that no pick face is left empty where stock exists in bulk, and releases Zone C to pickers. Any incomplete task, shortage in bulk or scanner fault is escalated before picking starts.

11. Goods requiring chilled storage in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C or hazardous materials in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F with its 4,000 kg limit are never used to replenish ambient pick faces in Zone C. Cold and hazmat replenishment follows PR-12 and PR-13 separately.

12. Speed limits apply to all replenishment movements: 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Seat-belt use on forklifts, high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zones B and C.

13. The maintenance technician is notified of any rack damage, beam deflection or floor obstruction found during replenishment. The affected bay or lane in Zone B or face in Zone C is blocked in the WMS until inspection is logged. All replenishment moves, exceptions and quarantine transfers are recorded in the WMS for handover under PR-15.

title: Order Picking in Zone C
text:
1. Order picking in Zone C is carried out under PR-04 and only from pick faces that have been replenished under PR-03. No picking begins on a shift until the shift supervisor has confirmed completion of replenishment and released Zone C to pickers.

2. Zone C occupies 1,200 m² and contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed exclusively from bulk storage in Zone B. Zone C holds no bulk reserve, no quarantine stock and no hazardous materials. Only booked stock directed by the WMS is present in Zone C.

3. Picking is scanner-driven. Ten pickers work in Zone C against WMS tasks issued to the 20 handheld scanners. The WMS directs the pick sequence by wave, customer order, aisle and face, and determines the shortest route through Zone C. No paper lists, verbal instructions or memory picks replace the scanner task.

4. Picking takes place only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. Floaters covering picking work only as pickers under the shift supervisor's direction and only on WMS tasks.

5. The picker logs on to the assigned scanner at the start of the shift, confirms the issued wave, and follows the directed sequence face by face. Flow racks are picked from the front pick side only; the rear replenishment side is not accessed by pickers.

6. At each face the picker scans the pick-face location label and then scans each item or case picked, in the quantity directed. The WMS verifies the SKU, batch or expiry where applicable, and quantity. The picker does not proceed to the next face until the scan is accepted by the system.

7. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed under PR-04. A pick that fails scan verification — wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong quantity or unreadable barcode — is stopped. The picker leaves the stock in place and reports the discrepancy immediately to the shift supervisor. No forced confirmation is permitted.

8. Picked goods are placed on the assigned outbound pallet, cage or tote for that order as directed by the scanner. The load is kept stable, within the pallet footprint and under the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load. Damaged, leaking, wet or suspect goods found at the face are not picked. They are segregated in place, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

9. Where the scanner reports a shortage at the face against expected quantity, the picker records nil or short pick on the scanner and notifies the shift supervisor. The supervisor checks the face, triggers a stock controller recount where needed and, if required, re-directs replenishment from Zone B. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

10. Pickers move goods within Zone C using 12 hand pallet jacks and 8 electric pallet jacks for small moves as directed. Counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are operated only by authorised forklift operators and are not used for picking tasks.

11. Pedestrian walkways in and around Zone C are physically separated by fixed yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide. Pickers use only these walkways and marked crossings between faces. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in Zone C.

12. Speed limits apply to all powered equipment in Zone C: 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps where applicable. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m are kept clear for replenishment and transfer to Zone D.

13. On completion of a wave, the picker presents the picked pallet or tote at the Zone C packing handover point, closes the WMS task on the scanner and returns the scanner to its charging location if required. All picks, short picks, exceptions and quarantine transfers are recorded in the WMS for handover under PR-15.

title: Scan Verification
text:
1. Every item picked in Zone C is scan-verified in the WMS under PR-04 before it is packed under PR-05. No picked item is packed, labelled or moved to Zone D without a successful scan verification on a handheld scanner.

2. Verification is carried out at the pick face by the picker using one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners. The picker scans the pick-face location label and then scans each SKU, batch or case picked, in the quantity directed by the WMS task. The system verifies SKU, batch, expiry where applicable, and quantity against the customer order.

3. Verification is face by face in the sequence directed by the WMS. The picker does not proceed to the next face until the current face is accepted by the system. The scanner displays accepted, short or rejected for each scan.

4. A successful verification requires three matches: location matches task, SKU and batch match order, and quantity matches directed quantity. Only when all three match does the WMS close the pick line and authorise packing for that line.

5. Any scan failure stops the process at that face. Wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong expiry, wrong quantity or unreadable barcode is not forced or manually overridden on the scanner. The picker leaves the stock in place, records the exception on the scanner as scan-failed, and reports immediately to the shift supervisor.

6. The shift supervisor decides the next action for a failed scan. This includes checking the face, confirming replenishment from Zone B, requesting a stock controller recount, or re-directing the pick to an alternative face. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

7. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found during verification are not scan-verified and not packed. They are segregated at the face, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The quarantine quantity and reason are recorded in the WMS.

8. Short picks are scan-verified as short. Where the face quantity is insufficient, the picker enters the actual quantity picked on the scanner and confirms short pick. The WMS logs the shortage, retains the order line as incomplete and notifies the shift supervisor for replenishment or order amendment.

9. Once all lines for an order or pallet are scan-verified, the WMS authorises packing and labelling for that pallet. Packing under PR-05 begins only after this authorisation. Goods are placed stable and within the pallet footprint, under the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load.

10. Labelling is applied only to scan-verified and packed pallets. The picker or packing staff scan the pallet licence plate and apply the WMS-generated label with customer, order and destination data. Hand-written labels or pre-printed labels that do not match the verified pallet record are not permitted.

11. The verified pallet is then closed in the WMS as ready for Zone D. The closure scan records picker name, scanner ID, date and time, and links the pallet to its order and outbound load. Only closed, scan-verified pallets are eligible for transfer to dispatch staging in Zone D.

12. All scan verifications, failures, short picks, quarantine moves and packing completions are recorded automatically in the WMS. The shift supervisor reviews verification exceptions during the shift and includes open verification faults, scanner defects and unresolved short picks in the PR-15 handover record.

13. Any scanner fault, label misprint or system rejection that prevents verification is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The affected pallet remains in Zone C, clearly separated and not moved to Zone D, until the fault is corrected and successful scan verification is completed on a serviceable scanner.

title: Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D
text:
1. Zone D is dispatch staging and occupies 900 m² directly in front of outbound doors 5 to 8. Zone D holds only outbound pallets for despatch under PR-05 and PR-06. No bulk storage, picking or quarantine stock is held in Zone D.

2. Packing, labelling and wrapping in Zone D take place only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. Work is directed by WMS tasks and the shift supervisor.

3. No pallet is packed in Zone D until its picks have been scan-verified in Zone C under PR-04. The WMS authorises packing only after successful verification of location, SKU, batch and quantity. Unverified pallets remain in Zone C and are not moved to Zone D.

4. Packing in Zone D is carried out at the packing stations and outbound pallets. Goods are placed stable, within the pallet footprint, with no overhang of racking or staging lanes. Every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg.

5. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found during packing are not packed. They are segregated in place, reported immediately to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The quantity and reason are recorded in the WMS.

6. Labelling is applied only to packed pallets in Zone D. Staff scan the pallet licence plate on the handheld scanner and apply the WMS-generated label showing customer, order, destination and pallet identity. Hand-written labels or labels that do not match the verified pallet record are not permitted.

7. A label that fails to scan, is misprinted or shows incorrect data is not used. The pallet remains in its packing lane in Zone D, clearly separated, and the fault is reported to the shift supervisor for reprint and rescan before release.

8. Wrapping is carried out in Zone D on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Only wrapped pallets are eligible for staging. Wrapping is performed by trained staff, with film containment to base and top, and with the label visible and scannable after wrapping.

9. Pallets that cannot be wrapped by machine due to size or stability are wrapped only by the approved manual method under PR-05 and checked by the shift supervisor. No unwrapped, partially wrapped or unstable pallet is placed in Zone D staging.

10. After wrapping, the pallet is closed in the WMS as packed, labelled and wrapped. The closure scan records name, date, time and outbound load reference. Only closed pallets are system-released for staging by door and load in Zone D.

11. Staging in Zone D is by outbound door 5 to 8 and by load as released by the dispatcher. Wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets only are placed in the marked staging lanes. Aisles, dock approaches, main transport aisles of 4.0 m and physically separated pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m are kept clear at all times.

12. Speed limits in Zone D are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone D, and forklift seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving.

13. Any scanner fault, wrapper defect, dock-leveller fault or shortage against the outbound load is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher. The affected pallet or lane remains on hold in Zone D and is not loaded until the fault is corrected and WMS release is confirmed for handover under PR-15.

title: Staging and Load Release
text:
1. Zone D occupies 900 m² directly in front of outbound doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 and is used solely for outbound staging under PR-06. No staging takes place outside Zone D and no bulk storage, picking or quarantine activity is carried out in Zone D.

2. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets are placed in Zone D. A pallet is eligible for Zone D only after it has been scan-verified in Zone C under PR-04 and packed, labelled and wrapped in Zone D under PR-05 and closed in the WMS. No unwrapped, unlabelled or unreleased pallet enters staging.

3. Staging in Zone D is by outbound door and by load. Each load is staged in its marked lane for doors 5 to 8, with pallets sequenced by drop and load order as shown on the WMS outbound manifest. No pallet is staged in the wrong lane, door approach or main transport aisle.

4. Every pallet staged in Zone D, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking or damaged pallets are not staged. They are segregated in place, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling and load release for the whole site. The dispatcher assigns every outbound carrier a specific door 5 to 8 and time slot, sequences loads by cut-off and carrier booking, and releases each load for loading. No door assignment is made or changed on the floor without dispatcher confirmation.

6. No loading begins without dispatcher release. Release is given only when the full load is wrapped, labelled, closed in the WMS and physically staged in Zone D in its correct lane, and the assigned vehicle is confirmed for that door and slot.

7. The shift supervisor controls floor preparation in Zone D. The supervisor confirms staging lanes are correct, quantities match the released load, labels are visible and scannable after wrapping, and the 4.0 m main transport aisles, dock approaches and physically separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways with fixed yellow barriers are clear.

8. Drivers report as directed and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to doors 5 to 8 only at the assigned time.

9. Loading at doors 5 to 8 begins only when the vehicle is correctly positioned at the assigned door, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller safely deployed by trained warehouse staff for that vehicle. Dock doors remain closed when not in active use.

10. Loading is carried out only by authorised forklift operators against the released WMS load, scanning each pallet licence plate and the door or load reference to confirm correct load. Any quantity, label or destination mismatch stops loading and is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher before further pallets are moved.

11. Once loading is complete, the load is closed on the scanner and sealed. Documents are completed with door number, carrier, load reference, pallet count, date, time and names of loader and dispatcher. No vehicle leaves Zone D without completed paperwork and dispatcher confirmation of release.

12. Speed limits in Zone D are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone D and forklift seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving.

13. Any shortage against the load, scanner fault, wrapper or leveller defect, or vehicle delay is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher. The affected lane remains on hold in Zone D and is not re-released until corrected. Open loads, waiting vehicles and release status are recorded for PR-15 handover.

14. Changes to Zone D lanes, door designations 5 to 8, time-slot arrangements, release process or staging rules require prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
text:
1. Every outbound pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This 1,000 kg limit is the basis for all vehicle load calculations, rack bay limits of 2,700 kg and staging rules in Zone D. No pallet above 1,000 kg is wrapped, staged or loaded.

2. The contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch are rated at 24,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions. The rating is determined by weight before floor space. At the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg, a trailer therefore takes at most 24 full-weight pallets. No trailer is loaded beyond 24,000 kg for any reason.

3. The 33 floor positions in a trailer are the physical floor count only. Where pallets weigh less than 1,000 kg, additional pallets may be loaded to use floor space, provided the total payload does not exceed 24,000 kg, the load is stable and within the pallet footprint, and the dispatcher has released the load.

4. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg payload on 6 floor positions. At the site pallet limit, the van takes at most one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet. No van is loaded beyond 1,200 kg.

5. Any consignment exceeding 1,200 kg, or requiring more than one full-weight pallet, does not go by van. It is assigned to a curtain-side trailer and loaded only at doors 5 to 8 under PR-06.

6. Outbound loading takes place only at doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller operated only by trained warehouse staff. No outbound loading is permitted at inbound doors 1 to 4.

7. The dispatcher owns transport booking and door allocation. The dispatcher assigns every outbound carrier a specific door 5 to 8 and time slot, sequences loads by cut-off, and releases each load from Zone D only when wrapped, labelled and closed in the WMS.

8. Outbound capacity per shift is fixed by doors and turn rate. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager.

9. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, 3 loads per door and 4 doors in use, the maximum outbound throughput is 12 trailer loads per shift. This equates to 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. This is the most that can be promised to a client for a single shift.

10. Staging in Zone D is planned against this maximum. Each load is staged by door and by drop sequence in its marked 900 m² lane in Zone D, with 4.0 m main transport aisles, physically separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways and dock approaches kept clear. No staging takes place outside Zone D.

11. No pallet is loaded without dispatcher release and WMS confirmation. Forklift operators scan each pallet licence plate and the door or load reference at doors 5 to 8. Any weight, label, quantity or destination mismatch stops loading and is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher.

12. Overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking or damaged pallets are not loaded to any vehicle. They are segregated in Zone D, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in the 60 m² cage in Zone F, meaning at most 4 full-weight pallets, is applied separately and no hazmat is loaded except from that cage under PR-13.

13. Load documents record carrier, door, time slot, trailer or van identity, pallet count, total weight and dispatcher release with date, time and names. No vehicle leaves the yard without completed paperwork and dispatcher confirmation. Any change to vehicle ratings, door allocation, turn rate or the 288-pallet shift maximum requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: Aisle Network and Walkways
text:
1. The internal circulation network provides physical separation between people and materials handling equipment at all times. Pedestrians and powered trucks use different, barriered routes. No shared unprotected route is permitted in the hall, in Zone F or at the docks.

2. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated from vehicle routes by fixed yellow barriers. The barriers are continuous, floor-fixed and impact-rated. No pallet, cage, packing material or waste is placed on, against or over a barrier and no gap is left open for convenience.

3. All separated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. The width is measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall. The walkways are the only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas in Zones A to F and to and from the office annex.

4. Walkways are permanently marked on the floor with solid white borders and green infill, signed overhead with pedestrian symbols and shown on the site plan at each entrance. Lighting, floor markings and signage are maintained so that the walkway is visible along its full length.

5. Main transport aisles provide the primary routes for counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and electric pallet jacks between Zones A to F and to and from dock doors 1 to 8. Every main transport aisle is 4.0 m wide, measured clear between racking, barriers or walls.

6. Main transport aisles are for through movement of loaded and unladen equipment only. No storage, staging, packing, quarantine or waste handling takes place in a main transport aisle, and the aisle is kept clear for its full 4.0 m width.

7. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. These aisles are for pallet put-away and retrieval in the 2,400-position high-bay racking only. They are not used as through-routes for general transport between zones unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

8. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, the meeting points are designed as marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Each crossing is signed, hatched on the floor and controlled by barriers, gates or speed reduction. No crossing is created without fixed signage and markings.

9. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m separated walkways and the marked crossings. Stepping outside a walkway into a main transport aisle of 4.0 m, into a rack aisle of 3.0 m or behind a vehicle at a dock is not permitted. Drivers and operators remain on vehicle routes and do not walk through walkways while driving.

10. Forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks remain on vehicle routes. Entry to a pedestrian walkway by any powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet is not permitted for any reason, including short cuts or temporary staging.

11. Physical separation is maintained at zone interfaces. Walkways connect Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services and control without requiring pedestrians to cross unprotected vehicle lanes. Doors to Zone E and gates to the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F open directly off walkways or controlled crossings.

12. All barriers, floor markings and crossing points are inspected as part of the monthly racking and equipment inspection by the maintenance technician and logged. Any damage to a yellow barrier, missing marking, obscured sign or blocked walkway is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and repaired before the route is returned to use.

13. Any change to the aisle network, walkway provision of 1.2 m, barrier type or position, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, or to the location of pedestrian zones, crossings or dock ramps requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan before use.

title: Speed Limits
text:
1. Three speed limits apply to every movement on site and are enforced on every shift without exception. No relaxation is permitted for workload, shift time, delivery pressure or vehicle type.

2. The limits are absolute maximums, not targets. Operators drive at a speed that allows the vehicle to stop safely within the visible clear distance, and always below the posted maximum for the area.

3. Inside the building the maximum speed is 10 km/h. This applies everywhere inside the hall, including Zones A to F, main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, packing areas and staging lanes, and to all powered equipment.

4. In the yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. This applies to the entire 3,500 m² fenced yard, circulation lanes, approaches to all eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height and the marked driver waiting area, and to all powered equipment and all visiting vehicles.

5. At all marked pedestrian zones, at all pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h. This applies whether the zone, crossing or ramp is in the hall or in the yard, and whether pedestrians are present or not.

6. The 5 km/h rule covers every place where people and trucks meet. This includes where the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers meet vehicle routes, gated crossings between zones, the interfaces at Zone E and Zone F, and the leveller and ramp area at doors 1 to 8.

7. The limits apply to every powered truck on site: the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, the 8 electric pallet jacks and any other powered handling equipment. Hand pallet jacks are pushed at walking pace only.

8. The limits apply equally to laden and unladen travel, to forward and reverse movement and to short repositioning moves. No higher speed is permitted for empty travel or for low loads.
