9. The limits are posted on signs at every hall entrance, at the yard gates, along main transport aisles and at each pedestrian zone, crossing and dock ramp. Floor markings and barrier signage indicate the start of each 5 km/h area. Signs are not obscured, removed or moved without approval.

10. Operators reduce speed before entering a lower limit area, not inside it. Braking, turning and cornering are completed under control and without skidding, wheel spin or load shift. Sounding the horn does not permit higher speed.

11. Overtaking is not permitted inside the building or at any 5 km/h area. In the yard overtaking is permitted only where visibility is clear, at or below the 15 km/h limit, and never at a crossing, ramp or pedestrian zone.

12. The shift supervisor enforces speed limits on the floor on every shift, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. Any observed breach, near miss or damage is reported immediately to the supervisor and recorded as an incident.

13. A vehicle found exceeding a limit is stopped and the task is reassigned until a safe method is confirmed. Repeated or serious breaches are escalated to the warehouse manager. Only the warehouse manager can change a limit, and any change requires updated postings, markings and briefing before use.

title: Pedestrian Safety Rules
text:
1. Pedestrian safety in Zones A to F, at the docks and in the yard is controlled under PR-11. The principle is full separation of people and powered equipment. Pedestrians and trucks never share an unprotected route.

2. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, without exception. This applies to all employees, the warehouse manager, visitors and contractors, in every zone, at every dock door and on every walkway. No person enters the hall without both items correctly worn.

3. Forklift operators and reach truck operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning moves in Zones B, C and D and on dock levellers at doors 1 to 8. No truck moves with the seat belt unfastened.

4. Pedestrians move only on the physically separated walkways protected by fixed yellow barriers. All separated walkways are 1.2 m wide measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall, marked with solid white borders and green infill, signed overhead and shown on the site plan at each entrance.

5. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are vehicle routes only. No pedestrian walks along, crosses or stands in a main transport aisle or rack aisle except at a marked pedestrian crossing. No powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet enters a 1.2 m pedestrian walkway for any reason.

6. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, movement is only at marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Each crossing is hatched on the floor, signed, and controlled by barriers or gates. No informal crossing is created or used.

7. At every marked pedestrian zone, at every pedestrian crossing and on every dock ramp the maximum speed for all powered equipment is 5 km/h, whether pedestrians are present or not. Inside the building the maximum elsewhere is 10 km/h; in the 3,500 m² fenced yard the maximum is 15 km/h. The 5 km/h areas start at the posted signs and floor markings.

8. Pedestrians have priority at crossings, but no crossing is started until the pedestrian has made eye contact with the operator and the vehicle has stopped. Pedestrians do not walk behind a vehicle at a dock, behind a reversing truck, or across a dock leveller unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

9. Drivers never enter the hall. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard and move to doors 1 to 8 only at the assigned time. Visitors and drivers on foot in the yard use only the marked walkways and crossings and obey the 5 km/h and 15 km/h limits.

10. Barriers, markings and signs are not moved, obscured or removed. No pallet, cage, packing material, waste or handling equipment is placed on, against or over a yellow barrier or on a walkway or crossing. The walkway is kept clear for its full 1.2 m width at all times.

11. The shift supervisor enforces PR-11 on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. The supervisor controls any temporary closure of a walkway, crossing or dock approach, informs the dispatcher immediately and provides an alternative barriered route before work continues.

12. Any incident, near miss, barrier damage, missing marking, obscured sign or blocked walkway is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The maintenance technician inspects barriers, markings and crossing points as part of the monthly inspection and logs every repair. The affected route is not returned to use until repaired.

13. Any change to PPE requirements, walkway provision of 1.2 m, barrier type or position, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, or to the location of pedestrian zones, crossings or dock ramps requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan before use.

title: Electric Fleet
text:
1. The site operates an all-electric materials handling fleet. No internal-combustion, LPG or diesel trucks are used in the hall or in the yard. All charging is from the designated charging area and only by trained staff.

2. The fleet consists of 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. No other pallet-moving equipment is held on site.

3. The 6 counterbalance forklifts at 2.5 t rated capacity are the general-work trucks. They carry out unloading and loading at the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, transport between Zones A to F on the 4.0 m main transport aisles, and put-away and retrieval to lower levels in Zone B.

4. The 4 reach trucks at 1.6 t rated capacity are for high-bay work in Zone B only. They serve the 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay racking and operate exclusively in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles and the adjoining transfer lanes.

5. Ratings of 2.5 t and 1.6 t are manufacturer rated capacities at rated load centre. The operational limit on site is lower and governs every lift: every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. No lift above 1,000 kg per pallet is permitted on any truck, including unladen-rated travel.

6. The 1,000 kg pallet limit is the basis for all storage limits in Zone B. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg total, and block stacking outside racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high. The WMS blocks any put-away that would exceed these limits.

7. The 8 electric pallet jacks are powered pedestrian or ride-on jacks for horizontal pallet moves. They are used for Zone A transfer to booking, replenishment support from Zone B to Zone C, and movement of wrapped pallets in Zone D to the staging lanes for doors 5 to 8.

8. The 12 hand pallet jacks are manual, non-powered jacks for small moves. They are used in Zone C for order tote and pallet positioning, in Zone F for packing and returns handling, and for short repositioning where powered equipment is not required. They are pushed at walking pace only.

9. The fleet does not include order-picking trucks, very-narrow-aisle trucks or tow tractors. Pickers do not drive counterbalance forklifts or reach trucks. Only forklift operators authorised personally by the warehouse manager drive the 2.5 t counterbalance and 1.6 t reach trucks.

10. All dock doors 1 to 8 are served by the counterbalance fleet and electric pallet jacks via their own dock levellers. Levellers are operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently assigned to that door. No driver operates MHE or levellers.

11. The site also holds 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D and 1 cardboard baler, plus 20 handheld WMS scanners shared across tasks. These are not MHE and do not lift loads. Wrapping, baling and scanning are carried out only by trained staff under PR-05 and PR-10.

12. Rated capacities are displayed on each truck's data plate and are not altered, uprated or derated locally. Any attachment, modification or repair affecting capacity, stability, braking or steering is reported to the shift supervisor and approved by the warehouse manager before return to service, with the maintenance technician logging the work.

13. No truck lifts more than its rated capacity and no pallet exceeds 1,000 kg. Any pallet indicating overweight, instability, collapse or unsafe wrapping is held in its zone and not lifted to height. It is segregated and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

14. Any change to fleet numbers, truck types, rated capacities of 2.5 t and 1.6 t, or to the 1,000 kg pallet limit requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to training, WMS limits and the posted fleet list before use.

title: Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. No person operates a counterbalance forklift rated at 2.5 t or a reach truck rated at 1.6 t without personal authorisation from the warehouse manager. No licence, no truck. Authorisation is granted under PR-10 only after verification of a valid forklift licence, training certificates and a supervised site assessment.

2. Authorisation is personal, in writing and specific to truck type. A person authorised for the 2.5 t counterbalance fleet is not automatically authorised for the 1.6 t reach trucks for high-bay work in Zone B, and vice versa. The warehouse manager signs the authorisation record with date, truck types and licence expiry.

3. The authorisation list is maintained by the warehouse manager and posted in the charging area and at the shift supervisor's station. It is the sole authority for who may drive. Eight forklift operators are normally listed; no other role, including inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns staff, dispatchers or floaters, drives those trucks unless personally added to the list.

4. No floater, visitor, driver or contractor operates any powered truck for any reason. The shift supervisor checks the list at the start of each shift 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and before any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager.

5. Authorisation lapses on licence expiry, training expiry or after any incident, near miss or failed reassessment. Operation ceases immediately until re-verification and re-authorisation by the warehouse manager. No temporary verbal permission is permitted.

6. Every truck receives a documented pre-use check before its first use each day. This applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts, the 4 reach trucks and the 8 electric pallet jacks. The 12 hand pallet jacks and the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers receive a visual check before first use on the same record.

7. The check is carried out by the assigned authorised operator using the PR-10 daily check sheet for that truck type. The check covers tyres and wheels, forks, carriage and chains, mast and hoses, brakes, steering, lights, horn, reversing alarm, seat belt, overhead guard, battery charge and containment, emergency stop and WMS scanner bracket where fitted.

8. No truck is started until the check is complete. A truck that has not been checked that day is not used for put-away in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, loading in Zone D or any other task, even for a short move on the 4.0 m main transport aisles or 3.0 m rack aisles.

9. The result is recorded with truck ID, date, time, operator name and signature, and countersigned by the shift supervisor. A pass records the truck as serviceable for that shift. Records are retained in the maintenance file under PR-10.

10. Any defect is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the truck is tagged out of service, keys removed and a do-not-use notice applied. The defect is logged as an incident, the maintenance technician is notified and the truck is not returned to service until repaired and cleared.

11. Defects affecting safety, capacity or stability — including brakes, steering, forks, chains, seat belt, battery, leveller interlock at the 1.2 m dock doors, or any damage affecting the 1,000 kg pallet limit or the 2,700 kg rack bay limit in Zone B — are escalated to the warehouse manager for approval before return to service. The repair is logged by the maintenance technician.

12. A truck that passes its daily check remains subject to continuous monitoring. Any fault arising during the shift is reported at once to the shift supervisor, the task is stopped and the truck is tagged out under paragraph 10. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m² yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps remain enforceable on all serviceable trucks.

13. Any change to authorisation requirements, licence standards, check sheets or truck numbers and ratings of 2.5 t and 1.6 t requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: Safe Operation
text:
1. All forklift and MHE movements are carried out under PR-10 by authorised operators only. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are operated only by forklift operators personally authorised in writing by the warehouse manager. No other role drives those trucks.

2. Seat belts are worn by every counterbalance and reach truck operator whenever the truck is moving. This applies to forward and reverse travel, laden and unladen moves, short repositioning in Zones A to F, on dock levellers at the 1.2 m doors, and in all aisles. No truck moves with the seat belt unfastened.

3. No passengers are carried on any truck. Only the operator is on the truck while it is moving, with high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear worn correctly in all operational areas.

4. Three speed limits apply to all powered equipment and are enforced on every shift without exception. Inside the building the maximum speed is 10 km/h. In the 3,500 m² fenced yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. At all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h.

5. The 10 km/h building limit applies everywhere inside the hall, including Zones A to F, main transport aisles, rack storage aisles, packing areas in Zone F, staging lanes in Zone D and the cold zone Zone E. The 15 km/h limit applies to all yard circulation lanes, approaches to doors 1 to 8 and the marked driver waiting area.

6. The 5 km/h limit applies at every place where people and trucks can meet, whether pedestrians are present or not. This includes where the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers meet vehicle routes, all gated crossings between zones, the interfaces at Zone E and at the 60 m² hazmat cage in Zone F, and the leveller and ramp area at each of the eight dock doors.

7. The limits apply equally to the 6 counterbalance forklifts, the 4 reach trucks and the 8 electric pallet jacks, laden or unladen. The 12 hand pallet jacks are non-powered and are pushed at walking pace only and never ridden.

8. Operators reduce speed before entering a lower limit area and complete braking and turning under control. The limits are absolute maximums; operators drive below the posted maximum where visibility, load, congestion or floor condition requires it.

9. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide measured clear between racking, barriers or walls. They provide the only through routes for powered trucks between Zones A to F and to and from doors 1 to 8. Main transport aisles are kept clear for their full 4.0 m width at all times with no storage, staging or temporary obstruction.

10. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. They are for pallet put-away and retrieval in the 2,400-position high-bay racking only and are served by the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t. Rack aisles are not used as through-routes for general transport unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

11. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated by fixed yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall. They are the only permitted pedestrian routes. No powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet enters a 1.2 m walkway for any reason, including short cuts.

12. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m separated walkways and marked crossings. No pedestrian walks along or stands in a 4.0 m main transport aisle or a 3.0 m rack aisle except at a marked crossing, and no pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at a dock or across a leveller unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

13. Every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg and each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg. No lift above 1,000 kg per pallet is permitted on any truck. Loads are carried low, tilted back and within the pallet footprint, with no overhang of racking or barriers.

14. The shift supervisor enforces seat-belt use, speed limits and aisle discipline on every shift 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. Any breach, near miss, barrier damage or blocked walkway or aisle is reported immediately to the supervisor, the task is stopped and the incident is recorded under PR-10.

title: Returns Intake and Inspection
text:
1. Returns handling is carried out under PR-07 in Zone F. All returned goods are received, recorded and inspected only in the returns inspection area in Zone F. No returns are received, inspected or stored in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E, and no returns are handled at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 days of the original delivery date only. The delivery date is taken from the outbound manifest and proof of delivery for that load. The 14-day window is counted as calendar days from delivery to presentation at the site.

3. Returned goods arrive at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4 at a time slot agreed with the dispatcher. The driver reports to the gate or dispatcher and waits with the vehicle or in the marked waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall and never move goods to Zone F.

4. Before unloading, inbound operators and the shift supervisor check the returns paperwork in Zone A: customer name, original order and outbound load reference, delivery date, SKU and quantity presented as return, and reason for return. No pallet is removed until the 14-day eligibility is confirmed.

5. Where the documents show the delivery was more than 14 days ago, where the customer or order cannot be matched, or where the quantity would breach site limits including the 1,000 kg pallet limit, the return is refused at the door. The refusal is recorded with date, time, door, carrier and reason and countersigned by the shift supervisor.

6. Accepted returns are moved directly to the returns inspection area in Zone F. They are booked in the WMS to returns status on arrival, with customer, original order, delivery date, return date, SKU, quantity, pallet identity and reason. They are physically separated, clearly signed as returns and not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

7. Every unit presented as a return is individually inspected in Zone F. Inspection is carried out by the 4 returns and packing staff under PR-07. No bulk acceptance, sample check or visual pass from a distance replaces unit-by-unit inspection.

8. Inspection is recorded against a checklist at the bench in Zone F: outer packaging condition, inner seal integrity, labelling and batch or expiry where applicable, leakage, wetting, contamination, odour, temperature condition for chilled goods from Zone E, and evidence of use, opening or tampering. The inspector's name, date and time are recorded with each pallet.

9. Any goods found damaged, leaking, wet, open, out-of-temperature or suspect during returns inspection are segregated immediately. They are booked to quarantine status in the WMS, labelled as quarantine, and moved to the physically separated quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. They are never held in the returns inspection lanes.

10. Hazardous materials presented as returns are identified at document check and inspection. They are handled only under PR-13, stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg cage limit, and never leave the cage until disposition is decided.

11. On completion of inspection, returns staff propose a disposition for each inspected quantity as restock, rework or scrap. The proposal is entered in the WMS with condition, quantity proposed for each route and reason, and the goods remain in Zone F pending approval. No returned goods are restocked, reworked or scrapped without that proposal.

12. No returned goods leave Zone F without final disposition approval. Goods remain clearly identified by returns or quarantine labels and WMS status until the shift supervisor approves the disposition under PR-07. Goods overdue for inspection or awaiting approval are escalated to the shift supervisor before end of shift.

13. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in Zone F. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all movements to and from Zone F. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

14. All returns receipts, 14-day eligibility checks, inspection records, quarantine transfers and proposed dispositions are logged in the WMS and retained for PR-15 handover. The shift supervisor reviews open returns, quarantine quantities and inspection exceptions on that shift and includes them in the handover record to the next supervisor.

title: Disposition and Write-Offs
text:
1. Disposition of all goods in quarantine in Zone F is decided under PR-07 for inspected returns and PR-09 for damaged goods. No goods leave quarantine for restock, rework or scrap without a recorded proposal and a formal approval. The warehouse manager signs off the final result for the site where thresholds require it.

2. The proposal is made in Zone F by the 4 returns and packing staff. For each inspected pallet or unit they enter in the WMS the proposed route: restock to available stock, rework in Zone F, or scrap for disposal, with quantity, condition, reason and inspector name, date and time.

3. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of every inspected return. The supervisor reviews the inspection record, checks 14-day eligibility and WMS status, and confirms restock, rework or scrap in the WMS before any physical move from Zone F. One supervisor is accountable for the decision on each shift.

4. Damaged goods found in any zone — Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone or Zone F itself — are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. They are booked in the WMS to quarantine status, labelled as quarantine and physically separated in the barriered quarantine area in Zone F.

5. Once in quarantine, damaged goods are assessed for write-off. The quantity, SKU, pallet identity, location found and nature of damage, wetting, leakage or seal failure are recorded with date and finder name for PR-09. Goods remain clearly identified and not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

6. Write-off approvals are by value threshold against the recorded stock value of the damaged quantity. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR. No threshold is aggregated to avoid escalation.

7. Approval is personal and recorded with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and quarantine reference in the WMS and on the paper quarantine record. A write-off without both entries is not actioned. Threshold approvals are not delegable.

8. Restock is approved only where inspection shows goods are intact, sealed, correctly labelled, within expiry and, for chilled goods, with no cold-chain breach between +2 °C and +8 °C. On supervisor approval, the WMS transfers the quantity from quarantine to available stock and directs put-away from Zone F to Zone B, Zone E or to pick faces as booked stock. No hand-written location is used.

9. Rework is approved for goods that can be made saleable in Zone F. On supervisor approval, goods remain in Zone F in the value-added packing area, clearly marked as rework, and are reworked only under PR-07. They are not restocked until reinspected, proposed again and re-approved as restock.

10. Scrap is approved where goods are unsaleable, contaminated, out-of-temperature or unsafe. On approval, the WMS books the quantity to scrap, the pallet is marked as scrap and held in quarantine pending disposal. Scrapped food, drugstore and hazmat quantities are segregated and never returned to Zone C or Zone D.

11. Hazardous materials follow the same quarantine route under PR-13. Damaged or suspect hazmat is moved to quarantine the same day, stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F and held against the 4,000 kg cage limit. No hazmat leaves the cage for restock or rework except under supervisor disposition and never without a safe-condition check.

12. No inventory adjustment for quarantine, scrap or restock is posted without a second count. Where a write-off quantity is disputed, the stock controller carries out the second count under PR-08 and the result is recorded before approval is given.

13. The maintenance technician is notified of any damage to racking, pallets or spill containment that caused quarantine, and logs the repair. The affected bay in Zone B with its 2,700 kg limit or lane in Zone F is blocked in the WMS until cleared by the warehouse manager.

14. Open quarantine quantities, proposed and approved dispositions, write-offs by threshold and scrap awaiting collection are reported to the shift supervisor during the shift and included in the PR-15 handover record with names, values and WMS references for the incoming supervisor.

title: Cycle Counting
text:
1. Cycle counting is carried out under PR-08 every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule. The counts run across all zones A to F and provide continuous verification that stock in the system is stock on the rack. No working day passes without cycle counts.

2. Two stock controllers own planning and execution of cycle counts. They prepare the daily count plan, issue WMS tasks to the handheld scanners and carry out first and second counts. They do not handle returns disposition or dispatch loading except through the count process.

3. The rotating schedule covers Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage of 2,200 m² with 2,400 high-bay positions, Zone C picking of 1,200 m², Zone D dispatch of 900 m², Zone E cold zone of 300 m² and Zone F services and control of 600 m² including the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage. Each zone is counted at least once in the rotation and high-movement areas in Zone B and Zone C are counted more frequently.

4. Counts are system-directed and blind. The WMS selects locations and SKUs for the day and generates count tasks on the 20 handheld scanners with location only. Quantity on system is not shown to the counter until the count is entered.

5. Counting takes place only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. The shift supervisor confirms that aisles, 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles are clear and that counting does not obstruct replenishment, picking or dock activity.

6. Counts are carried out on the scanner by scanning the location label and then counting and entering each pallet, case and unit at the location, including booked stock, quarantine in Zone F and hazardous stock in the hazmat cage against the 4,000 kg limit. Every pallet, load included, is checked as at most 1,000 kg where weight is relevant.

7. On entry of the count the WMS compares counted quantity to system quantity. A match closes the location as verified. Any discrepancy generates an immediate second-count task for the same location on a different scanner.

8. No adjustment is posted without a second count. The second count is carried out by the second stock controller or, where both are engaged, by the shift supervisor acting as second counter. The result is recorded with counter name, date, time and location.

9. Where first and second counts agree, the variance is confirmed. Where they disagree, the shift supervisor checks the location, verifies put-away, replenishment or quarantine moves from Zone B, C, E or F, and orders a third count before any adjustment is prepared.

10. In Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C counts are coordinated with the shift supervisor to minimise door open time. Short planned openings only are used, doors are closed between locations, and continuous monitoring and alarms remain active. No chilled pallet is removed from Zone E for counting.

11. Damaged, wet, leaking or suspect stock found during counting is not counted as available. It is segregated in place, reported immediately to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The location remains blocked pending inspection.

12. Adjustments arising from the daily cycle count are prepared by the stock controllers and approved only by the shift supervisor. Adjustments are posted in the WMS only after second count and approval, with reason, location, SKU, quantity, counter names and approver name retained.

13. All first counts, second counts, variances and approvals are logged in the WMS under PR-08. Open variances, blocked bays including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, and pending approvals are included in the PR-15 handover record between supervisors.

title: Annual Wall-to-Wall Stocktake
text:
1. A full wall-to-wall stocktake is carried out under PR-08 once per calendar year as a complete physical count of every pallet, case and unit on site. It verifies that the stock in the system is the stock on the rack across all six zones.

2. The site is shut down for the stocktake. No inbound receiving at doors 1 to 4, no put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F, no replenishment to Zone C, no order picking, packing or outbound loading at doors 5 to 8, and no returns intake takes place during the count. The dispatcher suspends all carrier bookings for the shutdown period.

3. The date and duration of the shutdown are set and approved personally by the warehouse manager and communicated in advance to all staff, clients and carriers. No wall-to-wall stocktake takes place without the manager present on site.

4. Before counting starts, the WMS is frozen at a cut-off time. All open put-away, replenishment, picking and dispatch tasks are closed or suspended, all pallets are left in their current locations, and Zones A to F, including the 2,400 high-bay positions in Zone B, the pick faces in Zone C, staging lanes in Zone D, the cold zone in Zone E and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, are made accessible and clear for counting.

5. The two stock controllers lead the count under the manager's direction, supported by trained counters from inbound, picking and returns teams. Counters are assigned to zones and aisles and work only on WMS count tasks issued to the 20 handheld scanners. No counter counts their own normal work area alone.

6. Counting is blind and location by location. The WMS generates count tasks by location with SKU not displayed. The counter scans the location label in Zone A, B, C, D, E or F and enters the counted quantity by SKU, batch and expiry where applicable. Every pallet, load included, is checked as at most 1,000 kg where relevant, and each rack bay in Zone B is checked against the 2,700 kg bay limit.

7. Where the WMS comparison shows a discrepancy between counted and system quantity, a second-count task is generated automatically for the same location. The second count is carried out by a different counter, normally the second stock controller or the shift supervisor acting as second counter.

8. No adjustment arising from the wall-to-wall stocktake is posted without a second count. Where first and second counts agree, the variance is confirmed; where they disagree, the warehouse manager orders a third count and investigation of movements, quarantine transfers and recent receipts before any adjustment is prepared.

9. Damaged, wet, leaking, open or suspect stock found during counting is not counted as available. It is segregated in place, reported to the warehouse manager and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Its location remains blocked until cleared.

10. Zone E is counted with doors closed between locations and continuous monitoring and alarms between +2 °C and +8 °C remaining active, with manual verification recorded. The hazmat cage in Zone F is counted in place against the 4,000 kg limit, with no pallet removed from the cage except under PR-13 supervision.

11. On completion of first and second counts, the stock controllers prepare a stocktake summary by zone, SKU and value, listing all variances, quarantine quantities and uncounted locations. The warehouse manager reviews the summary with the stock controllers and shift supervisors, checks second-count evidence and approves or rejects each proposed adjustment.

12. Only the warehouse manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results and any adjustment arising from it. Sign-off is personal, in writing, with name, date and time in the WMS and on the paper stocktake record. No adjustment from the annual stocktake is posted until that sign-off is given.

13. After sign-off, approved adjustments are posted in the WMS by the stock controllers, the freeze is lifted and normal operations in Zones A to F and at doors 1 to 8 are released by the warehouse manager. The full stocktake file, count sheets, second-count records, variance log and manager sign-off are retained for audit and briefed at the next PR-15 handover.

title: Adjustments and Recounts
text:
1. No inventory adjustment is posted in the WMS without a second count. This applies to every variance found during daily cycle counts, the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, quarantine transfers and any other stock check in Zones A to F. A single count alone never authorises a stock change.

2. An adjustment is the system change to quantity, SKU, batch, expiry or location to make the system match verified physical stock. Adjustments are prepared only by the two stock controllers. No other role prepares an adjustment, and no adjustment is posted by the counter who carried out the first count.

3. Where a first count entered on a handheld scanner does not match the system quantity, the WMS automatically generates a second-count task for the same location. The task shows location only, with no display of first count quantity or system quantity, and is issued to a different scanner.

4. The second count is carried out blind by a different person. It is performed by the second stock controller or, where both stock controllers are engaged, by the shift supervisor acting as second counter. The first counter does not recount their own location.

5. The second counter scans the location label in Zone A, B, C, D, E or F and enters the counted quantity by SKU, batch and expiry where applicable. The result is recorded with counter name, date, time and location before the WMS compares first and second counts.

6. Where first and second counts agree, the variance against the system is confirmed and the stock controllers prepare the adjustment with reason, quantity, location and both counter names. Where they disagree, no adjustment is prepared and the shift supervisor checks the location for recent put-away, replenishment or quarantine moves and orders a third count.

7. The third count is carried out by the shift supervisor or, during the annual stocktake, by the warehouse manager. The third result decides the verified quantity. If doubt remains, the pallet is segregated in place and the bay or lane blocked in the WMS until investigation is complete.

8. Damaged, wet, leaking or suspect stock found during any count is not counted as available and is not adjusted on the spot. It is reported to the shift supervisor, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and counted separately in quarantine status. Any write-off following quarantine is approved by value threshold under PR-09.

9. Counts in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C and in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg limit are recounted in place. No chilled or hazardous pallet is removed for recounting, doors in Zone E are closed between locations, and continuous monitoring and alarms remain active.

10. Adjustments arising from daily cycle counts are approved only by the shift supervisor after review of first count, second count and reason. The supervisor confirms the second count evidence in the WMS and approves with name, date and time before posting.

11. Adjustments arising from the annual wall-to-wall stocktake are approved only by the warehouse manager. No adjustment from the annual stocktake is posted until the manager has signed off the stocktake results in writing in the WMS and on the paper record with name, date and time.

12. Every adjustment is posted only after approval and is retained with full audit trail: location, SKU, quantity before and after, first count, second count, third count where taken, reason, preparer and approver. The WMS blocks any attempt to post without a second count task closed for that location.

13. Open variances, blocked bays including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, quarantine quantities and pending approvals are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors until cleared.

title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
text:
1. Racking and all handling and dock equipment are maintained under the control of the maintenance technician. The technician carries out planned checks, repairs and inspections and logs every repair and inspection in the maintenance record. No racking, truck, leveller, wrapper or barrier is returned to service after a defect affecting safety or capacity without approval.

2. High-bay pallet racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month. The inspection covers all racking in the 2,200 m² bulk area with its 2,400 pallet positions, including uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings, beam connectors and load signs. The check also covers designated block-stack areas for compliance with the 3-pallet-high and 4.0 m-high limits.

3. The monthly inspection is carried out only by the maintenance technician on a dated PR-10 inspection sheet. Results are recorded bay by bay against the 2,700 kg bay limit, with photographs of any damage, location references and a clear pass, monitor or block decision for each bay.

4. Any damage to uprights, beams, bracing or fixings, any deflection, impact mark or missing pin, or any defect affecting the 2,700 kg rack bay limit is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The bay is blocked in the WMS and physically barriered off. No put-away, retrieval or replenishment is directed to a blocked bay.

5. A blocked bay is not returned to use until repaired, re-inspected and cleared. Repairs affecting load capacity, beam levels or rack configuration require prior approval by the warehouse manager before return to service, with the approval, date and name retained in the maintenance file.

6. The monthly inspection also includes physical separation and dock equipment. The technician checks fixed yellow barriers for the 1.2 m walkways, main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m for clear width and markings, pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramp markings, and the eight dock levellers at 1.2 m height for structure, lip, controls and interlocks.

7. Materials handling equipment receives separate planned maintenance. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, 1 cardboard baler and 20 handheld scanners are maintained to manufacturer schedules, in addition to the documented daily pre-use check by the operator before first use each day.

8. Every repair and inspection is logged. The log records date, time, equipment or bay ID, zone, defect found, action taken, parts used, technician and operator names, downtime and, where required, warehouse manager approval for return to service. Daily check sheets, monthly racking sheets and repair logs are kept together for audit.

9. Any defect found during daily checks or during operations — including brakes, steering, forks, chains, mast, seat belt, lights, horn, battery or scanner bracket on trucks, or leveller, wrapper, baler or barrier faults — is reported at once to the shift supervisor, the truck or equipment is tagged out with keys removed and a do-not-use notice, and the maintenance technician is notified.

10. Defects affecting safety, capacity or stability are escalated to the warehouse manager. This includes any fault on the 1,000 kg pallet limit, 2,700 kg bay limit, 4,000 kg hazmat cage limit, load handling, braking, steering or leveller operation. No temporary fix or verbal clearance permits use.

11. The technician keeps the site plan, WMS location master and posted rack signs aligned. Any change to rack layout, bay capacity, aisle widths, barrier positions, leveller controls or fleet numbers and ratings requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the WMS locations and site plan before use.

12. Open defects, blocked bays, tagged equipment and pending approvals are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors. The incoming supervisor checks that blocked locations remain blocked in the WMS until the logged clearance is signed.

title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
text:
1. Cold-chain and hazmat response on site is controlled under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. PR-12 applies to the 300 m² cold zone Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C. PR-13 applies to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F and to any hazardous material found in Zones A to F.

2. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +8 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced, reset or ignored without investigation by the shift supervisor.

3. In addition to continuous monitoring, a manual temperature verification is carried out in Zone E on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. It is performed by the designated operator on a calibrated thermometer, recorded with date, time, measured temperature, name and signature, and countersigned by the shift supervisor. The log is retained in Zone E.

4. Any alarm, temperature excursion, door fault, icing, condensation, leakage or evidence of cold-chain breach is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The supervisor attends Zone E, secures the stock in place, closes the doors and prevents any despatch, replenishment to Zone C or put-away of new pallets to Zone E.

5. Affected pallets in Zone E are segregated in place, identified with quarantine labels and booked to quarantine status in the WMS where required. They are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 if damage or food-safety risk is suspected. No affected pallet is picked, packed or loaded until cleared.

6. The maintenance technician is notified at once and inspects the refrigeration plant, doors, seals, monitoring and alarm system, and logs every check and repair. Zone E is not used for new put-away until temperature is verified stable between +2 °C and +8 °C and the warehouse manager approves return to service for any defect affecting holding or alarms.

7. The hazmat cage in Zone F is a physically separated, signposted and locked enclosure of 60 m² with forced ventilation and spill containment. Total quantity in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. Incompatible hazard classes are segregated inside the cage as marked.

8. Access to the cage is restricted to authorised forklift operators and the shift supervisor, and the cage remains locked when not in active put-away or retrieval. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone F, with additional PPE as specified on the safety data sheet for the material. The 4,000 kg limit is displayed at the entrance.

9. A spill kit for the hazards stored is kept at the cage entrance in Zone F and is checked as part of the monthly inspection. Any spill, leak, damaged, wet or suspect hazmat pallet in any zone is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and made safe in place without touching leaking material.

10. Spill response is led by the shift supervisor under PR-13. The supervisor stops the source only if safe to do so, evacuates and barriers the area, ensures ventilation is running, prevents ignition sources and entry by unauthorised staff, drivers and pedestrians, and directs containment with the spill kit using correct PPE.

11. Contaminated materials, damaged pallets and used spill contents are segregated, labelled as quarantine and moved to the designated area of the cage or to quarantine in Zone F the same day. They are booked to quarantine status in the WMS and held against the 4,000 kg limit. No hazmat leaves the cage for restock, rework or scrapping except under supervisor disposition and after a safe-condition check.

12. Every cold-chain alarm, excursion and hazmat spill is recorded as an incident with date, time, zone, SKU and quantity, persons involved, action taken and supervisor name. The shift supervisor reviews the report on that shift, notifies the warehouse manager for any return-to-service decision and includes open alarms, quarantined quantities and cage status in the PR-15 handover.

13. The cage, ventilation, containment and Zone E refrigeration are not returned to normal use after a fault until inspected, logged by the maintenance technician and cleared by the warehouse manager. The clearance, date and name are retained in the maintenance file and WMS before new receipts are directed to Zone E or the cage.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Emergency evacuation and assembly on site is controlled under PR-14. PR-14 applies to every person on site in the hall, office annex and 3,500 m² fenced yard, including employees, visitors, contractors and drivers in the marked waiting area.

2. The alarm system provides audible evacuation signalling throughout the 6,000 m² hall, Zone E, Zone F including the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage, the office annex and the yard approaches to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m height. Alarms are tested to schedule and any fault is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician and logged.

3. On hearing the evacuation alarm, all work stops immediately in Zones A to F. Put-away in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picking, packing, wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and loading or unloading at doors 1 to 8 are left safe only if safe to do so, and dock levellers are left as found. No pallet, truck or document retrieval is permitted after the alarm.

4. Escape is only by the signed emergency routes leading to the final exits, using the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers, marked pedestrian zones and crossings where provided, and keeping the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles clear for movement. No one uses lifts, dock levellers or moves behind vehicles at doors to exit.

5. The shift supervisor is the incident lead for evacuation on that shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. The supervisor orders immediate evacuation where danger is confirmed, directs steady movement to the exits, prevents re-entry and takes charge at the assembly point.

6. The assembly point is at the marked area by the north fence in the yard. All employees, visitors and drivers assemble there by the north fence, clear of dock approaches, yard lanes and pedestrian crossings. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain worn. Drivers are accounted for by the dispatcher from the carrier assignment list for doors 1 to 8.

7. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is completed before anyone re-enters the building for any reason. The shift supervisor carries out roll call against the shift roster, visitor book, driver list and floater assignments, with names checked and missing persons reported at once.

8. No person leaves the assembly point by the north fence and no person re-enters the hall until the shift supervisor has completed roll call and confirmed the result. Where any person is unaccounted for, the supervisor informs the emergency services on arrival and no search is made inside the building by staff.

9. Re-entry takes place only after roll call is complete and the building is declared safe. The all-clear is given only by the emergency services or, for a drill or false alarm, by the warehouse manager or the shift supervisor acting on manager authority after verification by the maintenance technician where equipment, racking or refrigeration is involved.

10. An evacuation drill is carried out under PR-14 every quarter. The drill is scheduled by the warehouse manager, covers both 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shift patterns over the year, and includes full evacuation to the assembly point by the north fence, roll call by register and verification that no re-entry occurs before roll call is finished.

11. Each drill is recorded with date, time, shift, zones evacuated, time to complete evacuation, roll-call result, deficiencies found and names of the shift supervisor and counters. Deficiencies in routes, signage, barriers, lighting or walkway width of 1.2 m are notified to the maintenance technician and logged.

12. Every evacuation, drill or real, is reviewed by the shift supervisor on that shift. The review is logged under PR-14, open actions and equipment defects are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors, and any change to routes, exits, assembly point by the north fence or procedures requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.1 Speed Limits and Transport Routes
text:
1. Three speed limits are enforced on every shift without exception and apply to all powered equipment — the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks — and to all visiting vehicles in the yard. No higher speed is permitted for empty travel, low loads or delivery pressure. Hand pallet jacks are pushed at walking pace only.

2. Inside the building the maximum speed is 10 km/h. This limit applies everywhere inside the 6,000 m² hall, including Zones A to F, packing areas, staging lanes, main transport aisles and rack storage aisles.

3. In the yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. This limit applies to the entire 3,500 m² fenced yard, all circulation lanes, approaches to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height and the marked driver waiting area.

4. At all marked pedestrian zones, at all pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h. This lower limit applies whether the zone, crossing or ramp is in the hall or in the yard, and whether pedestrians are present or not.

5. The 5 km/h areas are where people and trucks meet. This includes every meeting point between vehicle routes and the physically separated pedestrian walkways, all gated crossings between zones, the interfaces at Zone E and Zone F, and the leveller and ramp area at each dock door 1 to 8.

6. The posted limits are absolute maximums, not targets. Operators must drive at a speed that allows the vehicle to stop safely within the visible clear distance and must reduce speed before entering a lower-limit area, not inside it. Sounding the horn does not permit higher speed.

7. The limits are signed at every hall entrance, at the yard gates and at each pedestrian zone, crossing and dock ramp. Floor markings and barrier signage indicate the start of each 5 km/h area. Signs are not obscured, removed or moved without approval.

8. Pedestrians and powered trucks use separate, barriered routes at all times. Main transport aisles provide the primary through routes for materials handling equipment between Zones A to F and to and from the docks. Every main transport aisle is 4.0 m wide measured clear between racking, barriers or walls.

9. Main transport aisles are for movement only. No storage, staging, packing, quarantine or waste handling takes place in a main transport aisle, and the aisle is kept clear for its full 4.0 m width.

10. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. These aisles serve the high-bay pallet racking only and are for pallet put-away and retrieval. They are not used as through-routes for general transport unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

11. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated from all vehicle routes by continuous fixed yellow barriers. All separated walkways are 1.2 m wide measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall and are the only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas.

12. No powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet enters a 1.2 m pedestrian walkway for any reason, and no pedestrian walks along or stands in a 4.0 m main transport aisle or a 3.0 m rack aisle except at a marked pedestrian crossing.

13. The shift supervisor enforces all three limits on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime. Any breach, near miss or damage is stopped immediately, reported to the supervisor and recorded as an incident. Only the warehouse manager may change a limit, aisle width or barrier position, and any change requires updated signs, markings and briefing before use.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.2 Segregated Pedestrian Walkways and Dock Discipline
text:
1. Separation of people and trucks is the governing rule in all Zones A to F, at the docks and in the yard. Pedestrians and powered equipment never share an unprotected route. Walkways for people and aisles for trucks are physically separated at all times.

2. The only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas are the physically separated walkways protected by continuous fixed yellow barriers. Every separated walkway is 1.2 m wide measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall, with solid white borders, green infill and overhead pedestrian signage.

3. Yellow barriers are floor-fixed, continuous and impact-rated. No pallet, cage, packing material, waste, stretch film or handling equipment is placed on, against or over a barrier, and no gap is left open for convenience. Walkways are kept clear for their full 1.2 m width at all times.

4. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m separated walkways and the marked crossings. No pedestrian walks along, crosses or stands in a main transport aisle or a rack storage aisle except at a marked pedestrian crossing, and no pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at a dock or across a dock leveller unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

5. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide measured clear between racking, barriers or walls and provide the primary through routes for the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks between Zones A to F and to and from the eight dock doors. No powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet enters a 1.2 m pedestrian walkway for any reason.

6. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide and are for pallet put-away and retrieval in the 2,400-position high-bay racking only. They are not used as through-routes for general transport unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

7. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, movement is only at marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Each crossing is hatched on the floor, signed and controlled by barriers or gates. No informal crossing is created or used.

8. At every marked pedestrian zone, pedestrian crossing and dock ramp the maximum speed for all powered equipment and visiting vehicles is 5 km/h, whether pedestrians are present or not. Pedestrians have priority at crossings but do not step out until eye contact is made and the vehicle has stopped.

9. The eight dock doors are dedicated by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading in Zone A. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading from Zone D. No inbound unloading is permitted at an outbound door and no outbound loading at an inbound door for any reason.

10. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot before arrival, and no vehicle approaches a door, is unloaded or is loaded without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher. Changes to door or slot are made only by the dispatcher.

11. Drivers report to the gate or dispatcher on arrival and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the 3,500 m² fenced yard. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to the door only at the assigned time.

12. No loading or unloading begins until the vehicle is correctly positioned squarely at the assigned 1.2 m door, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller safely deployed by trained warehouse staff for that vehicle only. Dock doors remain closed when not in active use and vehicles in the waiting area do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes.

13. Any temporary closure of a walkway, crossing, aisle or dock approach is controlled only by the shift supervisor, who informs the dispatcher immediately and provides an alternative barriered route before work continues. Any damage to a barrier, missing marking, obscured sign or blocked walkway is reported at once to the supervisor and repaired before the route is returned to use.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.3 Forklift Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. Only authorised forklift operators may drive powered handling equipment. No person operates a counterbalance forklift rated at 2.5 t, a reach truck rated at 1.6 t or an electric pallet jack without personal, written authorisation from the warehouse manager. No licence, no truck.

2. The powered fleet is all electric and limited to 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, and 8 electric pallet jacks for horizontal moves. The site also holds 12 hand pallet jacks which are manual, non-powered and pushed at walking pace only.

3. Authorisation is granted only after verification of a valid forklift licence, training certificates and a supervised site assessment under PR-10. The warehouse manager signs the authorisation with date, truck types and licence expiry. No temporary verbal permission is permitted.

4. Authorisation is personal and specific to truck type. Authorisation for the 2.5 t counterbalance fleet does not authorise high-bay work on the 1.6 t reach trucks, and vice versa. The authorised list is posted in the charging area and at the shift supervisor's station and is the sole authority for who may drive.

5. Eight forklift operators are normally listed as authorised. No other role — inbound operator, picker, stock controller, returns and packing staff, dispatcher, floater, visitor, driver or contractor — drives powered trucks unless personally added to the list by the warehouse manager.

6. The shift supervisor checks the authorisation list at the start of each shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, and before any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. No person not on the list is assigned a truck task in the WMS.

7. Authorisation lapses immediately on licence or training expiry, or after any incident, near miss or failed reassessment. Operation ceases until re-verification and re-authorisation by the warehouse manager.

8. Every powered truck receives a documented pre-use check before its first use each day. This applies to all 6 counterbalance forklifts, all 4 reach trucks and all 8 electric pallet jacks. The 12 hand pallet jacks and the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers receive a visual check before first use on the same record.

9. The check is carried out by the assigned authorised operator using the PR-10 daily check sheet for that truck type before the truck is started. It covers tyres and wheels, forks, carriage and chains, mast and hoses, brakes, steering, lights, horn, reversing alarm, seat belt, overhead guard, battery charge and containment, emergency stop and scanner bracket where fitted.

10. No truck is started or used for any move — including short repositioning on the 4.0 m main transport aisles or in the 3.0 m rack aisles — until the check is complete. The result is recorded with truck ID, date, time, operator name and signature and countersigned by the shift supervisor. A pass records the truck as serviceable for that shift.

11. Any defect is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The truck is tagged out of service, keys removed and a do-not-use notice applied. The defect is logged as an incident, the maintenance technician is notified and the truck is not returned to service until repaired and cleared.

12. Defects affecting safety, capacity or stability — including brakes, steering, forks, chains, seat belt, battery, dock-leveller interlock at the eight 1.2 m doors, or any damage affecting the 1,000 kg pallet limit or the 2,700 kg rack bay limit in Zone B — are escalated to the warehouse manager for approval before return to service. The repair is logged by the maintenance technician.

13. A truck that has passed its daily check remains subject to continuous monitoring. Any fault arising during the shift is reported at once to the shift supervisor, the task is stopped and the truck is tagged out. Enforceable limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all serviceable trucks at all times.

chapter_title: Chapter 2 - Personal Protection and Safety Accountability
title: 2.1 Mandatory PPE on the Warehouse Floor
text:
1. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for every person on the warehouse floor at all times, without exception. This applies to the entire 6,000 m² hall in Zones A to F, including receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch staging, the cold zone, services and control, packing benches and all dock leveller areas.

2. Mandatory means mandatory. The rule applies to the warehouse manager, shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, maintenance technician, dispatchers, floaters, visitors and contractors. No role, seniority or short visit exempts a person.

3. No person steps onto the warehouse floor, crosses a dock ramp or enters any operational aisle without both items correctly worn and fastened. A missing, unfastened or unsuitable vest or footwear is a stop-work fault and the person is not permitted in Zones A to F until corrected.

4. High-visibility vests are worn as the outer layer, fully zipped or fastened, with no covering garment that obscures visibility. Vests are kept clean, undamaged and clearly reflective. Personal high-visibility clothing is permitted only where it meets the same standard and is approved by the shift supervisor.

5. Class S3 safety footwear is safety footwear with enclosed toe protection, puncture-resistant sole, closed heel and water-resistant upper as required for the floor. Trainers, open shoes, low-cut shoes without safety rating or damaged footwear are not permitted on the floor for any reason.

6. Forklift and reach truck operators wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving. This applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and any other truck where a seat belt is fitted, including short repositioning moves, laden and unladen travel and movement on dock levellers at the eight 1.2 m doors. No truck moves with the seat belt unfastened.

7. The office annex and the marked driver waiting area in the 3,500 m² fenced yard are outside the mandatory PPE floor area, but any entry beyond the hall doors into the 6,000 m² hall requires full PPE before the threshold is crossed. Drivers never enter the hall and therefore are not issued floor PPE.

8. Additional PPE is required for specific tasks and zones in addition to vest and S3 footwear, not instead of them. In Zone E, held between +2 °C and +8 °C, insulated clothing is worn as directed for exposure time. In the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, additional PPE as specified on the safety data sheet for the material is worn by authorised operators and the shift supervisor.

9. Pedestrians and operators keep PPE correctly worn in all movement areas: on the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers, at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps where the 5 km/h limit applies, and in the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles.

10. PPE is inspected before each shift by the wearer and checked by the shift supervisor. Damaged, excessively worn, contaminated or non-compliant vests or footwear are removed from use immediately and replaced from approved stock. No repair with tape, pins or makeshift fastening is permitted.

11. The shift supervisor enforces PPE on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. Any breach is stopped at once, recorded as an incident and briefed at handover under PR-15.

12. Only the warehouse manager may change the PPE standard for the warehouse floor. Any change requires updated instruction, briefing and signage at all hall entrances before it takes effect.

chapter_title: Chapter 2 - Personal Protection and Safety Accountability
title: 2.2 Roles and Supervision for Safety
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for safety on the whole site. This covers operations, safe working in all Zones A to F, the 3,500 m² fenced yard and the eight dock doors at 1.2 m height, and all final sign-offs. No safety activity takes place outside the manager's authority.

2. The manager holds all site-level approvals. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift and reach truck operators in writing after licence, training and site assessment, approves overtime including Saturday morning overtime, and signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results and any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR.

3. Only the warehouse manager approves changes to fixed site standards. This includes hall or yard layout, zone boundaries and zone use, the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage location and its 4,000 kg limit, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, pedestrian walkway provision of 1.2 m with fixed yellow barriers, dock designations and speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

4. One shift supervisor is in charge of the floor on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime. The site never operates without its supervisor present. The morning and afternoon supervisors provide continuous cover Monday to Friday.

5. The shift supervisor directs all floor staff on that shift across Zones A to F, including forklift operators, inbound operators in Zone A, pickers in Zone C, returns and packing staff in Zone F, floaters and the maintenance technician for immediate tasks. Task allocation and sequencing are controlled by the supervisor.

6. The shift supervisor is the incident lead on that shift. All injuries, near misses, damage to racking or equipment including the 2,700 kg bay limit in Zone B, temperature alarms in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, and spills in the hazmat cage in Zone F are reported immediately to the supervisor, who secures the area and initiates response under PR-09, PR-13 and PR-14.

7. The shift supervisor enforces daily safety standards on the floor. This includes high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear for everyone in the hall, seat-belt use whenever a truck is moving, the three speed limits, and use of the physically separated 1.2 m walkways. Any breach is stopped at once and recorded as an incident.

8. Approvals on the floor are by fixed threshold and are not delegable. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR after same-day quarantine in Zone F, the final disposition of inspected returns in Zone F as restock, rework or scrap, and reviews every incident report arising on that shift.

9. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport and assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot — doors 1 to 4 inbound only and doors 5 to 8 outbound only — and releases every outbound load from Zone D. No door change or release is made on the floor without dispatcher confirmation.

10. The maintenance technician is accountable for logging every repair and inspection of materials handling equipment, racking and dock levellers. Any defect affecting load capacity, the 1,000 kg pallet limit, braking, steering, barriers or leveller operation is reported to the shift supervisor and is not returned to service without warehouse manager approval.

11. Role boundaries are fixed. Forklift operators drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and electric pallet jacks. Inbound operators work only in Zone A, pickers only in Zone C on scanner tasks, stock controllers own cycle counts and second counts, and returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose disposition.

12. If doubt arises on authority or a safe method of work, the shift supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager before action. Approvals are recorded with name, date and value or quantity, and open incidents, defects and approvals are handed over at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)
text:
1. Zone E is the physically segregated chilled storage enclosure of 300 m² within the 6,000 m² hall, held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C. Zone E is insulated, with self-closing doors and no other use, and stores only booked goods requiring chilled conditions under PR-12.

2. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +8 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced, reset or ignored without investigation by the shift supervisor.

3. In addition to continuous monitoring, a manual temperature verification is carried out in Zone E on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime. It is performed by the designated operator on a calibrated thermometer with date, time, measured temperature, name and signature, and countersigned by the shift supervisor. The log is retained in Zone E.

4. Entry to Zone E is restricted to authorised operators acting on a WMS task for put-away, replenishment or inspection, and to the shift supervisor. No other person enters Zone E, and no chilled pallet is moved without a released WMS task to a directed vacant location.

5. Doors to Zone E remain closed except during active task execution. Doors are opened only to move a pallet or person through, are not wedged or held open, and are closed immediately after. No pallet is staged in doorways, against evaporators or across aisles.

6. Exposure time in Zone E is minimised. Personnel and electric equipment enter only to complete the directed task and then exit. Electric pallet jacks used in Zone E are rated for chilled operation. No one remains in Zone E longer than the task requires.

7. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone E at all times. In addition, insulated clothing is worn as directed for cold exposure. No person enters Zone E without both mandatory items plus cold PPE correctly worn and fastened.

8. Speed limits apply in Zone E as inside the building: 10 km/h maximum. At the marked pedestrian zone and crossing at the Zone E doors the maximum is 5 km/h, whether pedestrians are present or not. Operators reduce speed before the zone, not inside it.

9. Pedestrians reach Zone E only by the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and the marked crossing at the Zone E doors. No pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at the Zone E interface and no powered truck enters the pedestrian walkway for any reason.

10. Any temperature alarm, excursion outside +2 °C to +8 °C, door fault, icing, condensation, leakage or evidence of cold-chain breach is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The supervisor attends, secures stock in place, closes doors, and prevents any picking in Zone C, packing or dispatch of affected pallets.

11. Affected pallets are segregated in place, identified with quarantine labels and, where required, booked to quarantine status. They are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 and are not picked, replenished, packed or loaded until cleared.

12. No new put-away to Zone E is permitted during an active alarm or verified excursion. Zone E is not used for new receipts until temperature is verified stable between +2 °C and +8 °C, the maintenance technician has inspected the refrigeration plant, doors, seals, monitoring and alarms, and any defect affecting holding or alarms is cleared by the warehouse manager.

13. The maintenance technician logs every inspection, repair and temperature-system check for Zone E. An evacuation alarm or cold-related incident is recorded as an incident with date, time, quantity and supervisor name, reviewed by the shift supervisor on that shift and handed over under PR-15 before staff re-enter.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.2 Hazmat Cage and Spill Response (Zone F)
text:
1. All hazardous materials on site are stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F. No hazmat is stored in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E or anywhere else in the 600 m² Zone F outside the cage, even temporarily.

2. The cage is a physically separated, signposted and locked enclosure within Zone F with forced ventilation and integral spill containment. It is kept locked at all times except during active put-away or retrieval on a released task, and access is restricted to authorised forklift operators and the shift supervisor.

3. Total quantity in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at any time. Every pallet on site, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg, so at most 4 full-weight pallets may be in the cage at once. The 4,000 kg limit is displayed at the cage entrance and on the Zone F site plan.

4. Put-away to the cage is permitted only from Zone A after document check, count and inspection under PR-01 and PR-13. Quantity is checked against the 4,000 kg limit before booking in the WMS, and the WMS blocks any receipt or put-away that would exceed the limit. Excess remains in Zone A for shift supervisor decision on partial acceptance or refusal.

5. Pallets in the cage are stored only in marked hazmat positions, stable, intact, correctly labelled and fully within the pallet footprint. Incompatible hazard classes are segregated inside the cage as marked. No pallet is placed against ventilation openings, doors, spill bunds or outside marked positions.

6. Transport to and from the cage is by authorised forklift operators only, against a released WMS task on a handheld scanner. The 4,000 kg limit applies to storage and to any staged load for dispatch; no hazmat is loaded to a vehicle except from the cage under PR-13 and dispatcher release.

7. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in Zone F. Inside the cage and during any hazmat handling, additional PPE as specified on the safety data sheet for the material is worn correctly in addition to vest and S3 footwear, not instead of it.

8. A spill kit suitable for the hazards stored is kept at the cage entrance in Zone F, clearly signed and accessible. It is checked as part of the monthly inspection by the maintenance technician and any used or missing contents are replaced immediately.

9. Any spill, leak, damaged, wet, open or suspect hazmat pallet in any zone is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The pallet is made safe in place without touching leaking material, and no one moves it until the supervisor attends.

10. Spill response is led by the shift supervisor under PR-13. The supervisor stops the source only if safe to do so, evacuates and barriers the area, ensures forced ventilation is running, eliminates ignition sources, prevents entry by unauthorised staff, drivers and pedestrians, and directs containment and clean-up with the spill kit using correct SDS PPE.

11. Contaminated materials, damaged pallets and used spill contents are segregated, labelled as quarantine and moved to the designated quarantine area of Zone F or held in the cage the same day they are found under PR-09. They are booked to quarantine status in the WMS and remain counted against the 4,000 kg cage limit until disposed.

12. No hazmat leaves quarantine for restock, rework or scrap without shift supervisor disposition after a safe-condition check. Hazmat is never returned to Zone C pick faces or Zone D staging unless formally cleared, and no hazmat is held in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C.

13. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and the Zone F access apply to all movements to and from the cage. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and the marked crossing at Zone F.

14. Every spill, leak or hazmat damage is recorded as an incident with date, time, SKU, quantity, persons involved, PPE used and action taken. The shift supervisor reviews the report on that shift, notifies the warehouse manager, and includes cage quantity, quarantine stock and open actions in the PR-15 handover.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
text:
1. Every pallet on site, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This pallet limit governs all storage capacities on site, including rack bay limits in Zone B and the hazmat cage limit in Zone F. No pallet above 1,000 kg is accepted, booked or stored.

2. High-bay pallet racking in Zone B provides 2,400 pallet positions within 2,200 m². Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total. The bay limit is displayed on the bay load sign and in the WMS.
