3. The 2,700 kg bay limit determines how many pallets a bay can hold. At the site limit of 1,000 kg, a bay holds at most 2 full-weight pallets. A third full-weight pallet would be 3,000 kg and exceeds the bay limit. Lighter pallets may allow more units only if the total bay weight remains at or below 2,700 kg and all positions are vacant and serviceable.

4. Put-away to Zone B is permitted only to a directed vacant position within the bay limit. The WMS blocks any put-away that would exceed 2,700 kg in the bay and blocks any move to a damaged, reserved or blocked bay. No hand-written location or verbal instruction replaces the system task.

5. Where block stacking is used outside racking, stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high including the pallets, whichever is reached first. No block stack exceeds either limit for any reason, including short-term staging.

6. Block stacking is permitted only in designated block-stack areas. No block stack is placed in a 3.0 m rack storage aisle, against rack uprights, across a 4.0 m main transport aisle, against barriers, doors, evaporators or fire exits, or on any pedestrian route.

7. Only stable, undamaged and correctly wrapped pallets are stored in racking or block stacks, with the load fully within the pallet footprint and with no overhang of beams, uprights or adjacent pallets. No leaning, collapsed or unstable pallet is stored at height.

8. Any pallet found overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking, wet or with damaged wrapping or pallets is not put away and not re-stored. It is made safe in place, segregated, reported immediately to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The bay or stack location is left empty and blocked until cleared.

9. The same weight logic applies to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F. Total quantity in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at any time, so at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets may be in the cage at once. The WMS blocks any receipt that would exceed 4,000 kg. No hazmat is stored outside the cage.

10. Racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month by the maintenance technician on a dated sheet, bay by bay against the 2,700 kg limit. Uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings, beam connectors and load signs are checked, with photographs of damage and a pass, monitor or block decision.

11. Any damage to uprights, beams, bracing or fixings, any deflection, impact mark or missing pin, or any defect affecting the 2,700 kg bay limit or the 4.0 m stack height is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The bay or stack area is blocked in the WMS and physically barriered off. No put-away, retrieval or replenishment is directed there.

12. A blocked bay or stack area is not returned to use until repaired, re-inspected and logged. Any repair affecting load capacity, beam levels or rack configuration requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before return to service, with date, name and approval retained in the maintenance file.

13. No storage takes place outside marked rack positions and designated block-stack areas. No attachment, modification or change to rack layout, bay capacity, stacking height or designated areas is made without prior approval by the warehouse manager and update to the posted site plan and WMS locations before use.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.1 Incident Reporting and Review
text:
1. An incident is any injury to a person, near miss between people and equipment, damage to racking, pallets or equipment, spill or leak in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, temperature alarm or excursion in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, breach of the 10 km/h, 15 km/h and 5 km/h speed limits, or any departure from PR-09, PR-13, PR-14 and this Instruction. No incident is treated as minor.

2. Every person who is involved in, witnesses or discovers an incident reports it immediately to the shift supervisor on that shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. Reporting is verbal and in person or by radio, not delayed to the end of the task.

3. Work at the affected location stops at once. The person reporting makes the area safe only if safe to do so, leaves equipment and stock as found, and prevents other pedestrians, drivers and trucks from entering. No clean-up, re-stacking or movement to quarantine in Zone F is undertaken until the supervisor attends.

4. The shift supervisor is the incident lead on that shift. One supervisor is present on every shift and takes charge of all injuries, near misses, rack or equipment damage including any defect affecting the 2,700 kg bay limit in Zone B, temperature alarms in Zone E and spills in the hazmat cage. No one else assumes the lead.

5. The supervisor attends immediately, secures and barriers the area, checks for injuries and arranges first aid, ensures the 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and the 4.0 m main transport aisles remain clear for emergency access, and prevents re-entry to the affected bay, aisle, dock approach or cage until cleared.

6. The supervisor initiates the correct response under procedure: PR-09 for damaged goods and quarantine to Zone F the same day, PR-13 for hazmat spill response with the spill kit at Zone F and forced ventilation in the cage, and PR-14 for evacuation to the assembly point by the north fence where required. The supervisor ensures high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear remain worn throughout.

7. An incident report is completed on the same shift by the supervisor with the persons involved. It records date, time, zone and exact location, names of persons involved and witnesses, truck or equipment ID where applicable including the 2.5 t counterbalance and 1.6 t reach trucks, description of what happened, immediate action taken and photographs where there is damage to racking, barriers, levellers or stock.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising on that shift before the shift closes. Review includes checking facts with witnesses, confirming that quarantine moves, bay blocks in the WMS, tag-outs of trucks and notifications to the maintenance technician and dispatcher have been made, and deciding corrective action.

9. Corrective action is issued by the supervisor on review and may include re-briefing, re-training, bay or aisle closure, equipment repair, replacement of barriers or signage, or referral to the warehouse manager. No affected bay in Zone B, no tagged truck and no hazmat cage access is returned to service without the required inspection, log entry and manager approval where capacity or safety is affected.

10. The warehouse manager is notified of all lost-time injuries, any rack impact requiring bay closure, any hazmat spill and any cold-chain breach in Zone E. The manager confirms the close-out of serious incidents, monitors trends across shifts and holds final authority for any change to site standards arising from investigation.

11. No fault is used as a reason to delay reporting. Any breach, near miss or barrier damage is recorded as an incident even where no injury or damage resulted. Reprisal for reporting is not permitted.

12. All incident reports, review notes, photographs, maintenance logs and corrective-action records are retained in the incident file and in the WMS where applicable. They are kept for audit and made available to the incoming supervisor at handover.

13. Open incidents, blocked bays, tagged equipment, quarantine quantities and pending corrective actions are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors at 14:00 and 22:00. The incoming supervisor verifies that blocks and tag-outs remain in place until the logged clearance is signed.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns
text:
1. Any damaged, leaking, wet, open, collapsed or suspect pallet or unit found in any zone — Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone or Zone F itself — is moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day it is found under PR-09. No damaged stock remains in its original zone overnight.

2. Quarantine is located in Zone F within the 600 m² services and control area. It is a physically separated, barriered and clearly signed area, distinct from packing, returns inspection and the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage. Goods in quarantine remain clearly identified by quarantine labels and WMS quarantine status and are not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

3. On finding damage, the finder stops work at that location, makes the area safe if safe to do so and reports immediately to the shift supervisor. The supervisor attends, secures and barriers the bay, lane or face, and directs transfer to Zone F. No sorting, re-stacking or disposal takes place at the original location.

4. Transfer to quarantine is booked in the WMS to quarantine status before the pallet leaves its zone. The record includes date, zone and exact location found, SKU, batch and expiry where applicable, quantity, pallet identity, nature of damage and finder name. The pallet is labelled as quarantine and placed only in the designated quarantine lanes in Zone F.

5. Damaged hazardous materials are quarantined the same day under PR-09 and PR-13. They are stored only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F and remain counted against the cage limit of 4,000 kg, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. No damaged hazmat is held outside the cage.

6. Damaged chilled goods from Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C are segregated in place, booked to quarantine status where required and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day. They are not returned to Zone E pending decision and are not picked, packed or loaded until cleared.

7. No goods leave quarantine without a recorded approval. Write-offs for damaged goods are approved strictly by value threshold. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR.

8. Approval is personal and entered in the WMS and on the paper quarantine record with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and quarantine reference. Thresholds are not aggregated or split to avoid escalation, and approvals are not delegable. No inventory adjustment for quarantine or scrap is posted without a second count.

9. Returns are handled only in Zone F under PR-07. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 days of the original delivery date. Returns are received at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4, checked for eligibility in Zone A and moved directly to the returns inspection area in Zone F, booked to returns status and physically separated from quarantine.

10. Every unit returned is individually inspected in Zone F by returns and packing staff against a checklist of packaging, seal, labelling, leakage and temperature condition. Goods found damaged, leaking, wet or out-of-temperature during inspection are segregated immediately, booked to quarantine status and moved to the quarantine area the same day. They are never held in the inspection lanes.

11. On completion of inspection, returns staff propose a disposition for each quantity as restock, rework or scrap, with condition, quantity and reason entered in the WMS. Goods remain in Zone F pending approval and are not restocked, reworked or scrapped without a proposal.

12. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of all inspected returns before any move from Zone F. Restock is approved only where goods are intact, sealed, correctly labelled and within cold-chain where applicable; rework remains in the value-added packing area in Zone F until reinspected; scrap is booked to scrap and held in quarantine pending disposal.

13. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for all quarantine and returns handling in Zone F. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and the Zone F access apply to all movements, with pedestrians using only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways. Open quarantine quantities, proposals and approvals are included in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.3 Evacuation, Alarms and Drills
text:
1. Emergency evacuation and assembly is controlled under PR-14. It applies to every person in the 6,000 m² hall, the office annex and the 3,500 m² fenced yard — employees, visitors, contractors and drivers in the marked waiting area — in Zones A to F, including Zone E and the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F.

2. The alarm system provides audible evacuation signalling throughout the hall, Zone E, Zone F, the office annex and the yard approaches to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m height. Alarms are tested to schedule and any fault, failed sounder or missing signage is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician and logged.

3. On hearing the evacuation alarm, all work stops immediately in Zones A to F. Put-away in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picking, packing, wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and loading or unloading at doors 1 to 8 are left safe only if safe to do so, with dock levellers left as found. No pallet, truck, scanner or document retrieval is permitted after the alarm.

4. Escape is only by the signed emergency routes to the final exits, using the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and the marked pedestrian zones and crossings. The 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles are kept clear for movement. No one uses lifts, dock levellers or passes behind a vehicle at a door to exit.

5. The shift supervisor is the incident lead for evacuation on that shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. One supervisor is present on every shift. The supervisor orders immediate evacuation where danger is confirmed, directs steady movement to the exits, checks that toilets, Zone E and the hazmat cage are cleared, and prevents re-entry.

6. The assembly point is the marked area by the north fence in the yard, clear of dock approaches, yard lanes and pedestrian crossings. All persons move directly there and remain together. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear remain worn. Drivers are accounted for by the dispatcher from the carrier assignment list for doors 1 to 8.

7. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is completed before anyone re-enters the building for any reason. The shift supervisor carries out roll call against the shift roster, visitor book, driver list and floater assignments for that shift. Names are checked individually and any missing person is reported to the emergency services at once. No search inside the building is made by staff.

8. No person leaves the assembly point by the north fence and no person re-enters the hall until the shift supervisor has completed roll call and confirmed the result. This prohibition applies to employees, managers, drivers and visitors. Where any person is unaccounted for, the supervisor informs the emergency services on arrival and follows their direction.

9. Re-entry takes place only after roll call is complete and the building is declared safe. The all-clear is given only by the emergency services or, for a drill or false alarm, by the warehouse manager or the shift supervisor acting on manager authority after verification by the maintenance technician where racking, equipment, refrigeration in Zone E or ventilation in the hazmat cage is involved.

10. An evacuation drill is carried out under PR-14 every quarter. The drill is scheduled by the warehouse manager, covers both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shift patterns over the year, and includes full evacuation from all Zones A to F to the assembly point by the north fence, roll call by register and verification that no re-entry occurs before roll call is finished.

11. Each drill is recorded with date, time, shift, zones evacuated, time to complete evacuation, roll-call result, deficiencies found and names of the shift supervisor and counters. Deficiencies in routes, signage, lighting, barriers or walkway width of 1.2 m, blocked aisles or failed alarms are notified to the maintenance technician immediately and logged.

12. Every evacuation, drill or real, is reviewed by the shift supervisor on that shift under PR-14. Open actions, equipment defects and blocked bays are included in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00 between supervisors until cleared. Any change to escape routes, exits, the assembly point by the north fence or PR-14 requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
text:
1. You are the warehouse manager and the single accountable owner of the Harborwick 3PL site. You are accountable for the whole site — all operations in Zones A to F, safety in the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 fenced yard, inventory accuracy, and all final sign-offs. No activity takes place outside your authority.

2. You are the only person who authorises new forklift and reach truck operators. Authorisation is personal and in writing after verification of licence, training certificates and a supervised site assessment under PR-10. No person operates the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t or the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t without your signature, with date, truck type and licence expiry recorded.

3. You are the only person who approves overtime. This covers any extension beyond 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday and any Saturday morning overtime in peak season. No other role calls staff in, extends a shift or schedules weekend work. Every approval is recorded with date, period, roles required and reason.

4. You sign off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08. You set and approve the shutdown date and duration, are present on site for the count, review the stocktake summary with the two stock controllers, and provide personal written sign-off of the results and any adjustment arising from it in the WMS and on the paper record before the system is updated.

5. You approve all damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR after same-day quarantine in Zone F under PR-09. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor. You do not delegate write-offs above threshold, and no adjustment is posted without a second count.

6. You approve the final return to service of any rack bay, handling equipment or dock installation where capacity or safety is affected. This includes any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, any defect affecting the 1,000 kg pallet limit or 4,000 kg hazmat cage limit in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F, and any fault on braking, steering, barriers or dock levellers at the eight 1.2 m doors.

7. You own fixed site standards and no change is made without your prior approval. This includes hall or yard layout, zone boundaries and zone use for Zones A 800 m2, B 2,200 m2, C 1,200 m2, D 900 m2, E 300 m2 and F 600 m2, the location and size of the hazmat cage, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, pedestrian walkway provision of 1.2 m with fixed yellow barriers, dock designations for doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound, time-slot arrangements, and speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

8. You approve any change to vehicle and throughput assumptions before it is promised to a client. This includes the 1,000 kg pallet limit, trailer rating of 24,000 kg on 33 positions taking 24 full-weight pallets, van rating of 1,200 kg on 6 positions taking one full-weight pallet, and the site maximum of 288 full-weight pallets per shift from 4 outbound doors at 3 loads per shift.

9. You ensure periodic duties are carried out to schedule. You ensure cycle counts run every working day on the rotating zone schedule under PR-08, racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month, manual temperature verification in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C is carried out each shift with continuous monitoring and alarms, and an evacuation drill to the assembly point by the north fence is carried out every quarter under PR-14.

10. You ensure the fifteen procedures PR-01 to PR-15 are applied and that Zone F holds only quarantine, returns and hazmat in the cage, Zone E holds only chilled booked stock, and Zone D holds only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets. You remain accountable for handover under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00.

11. Your approvals are recorded with name, date and value or quantity and are not delegable except where a threshold expressly assigns a decision to the shift supervisor or dispatcher. Where doubt arises on authority, the shift supervisor escalates to you before action, and where this manual conflicts with the brief from the owner, the brief prevails.

title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
text:
1. You are the shift supervisor in charge of the floor on your shift. You run the shift from 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, and during any Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. The site never operates without you present and no work starts until you are on the floor.

2. You direct all floor staff on that shift across Zones A to F. This includes the inbound operators in Zone A at doors 1 to 4, forklift operators on the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the electric pallet jacks, pickers in Zone C, returns and packing staff in Zone F, stock controllers for counts, the maintenance technician for immediate tasks, and the two floaters covering absence.

3. You control sequencing and work allocation on the floor. You issue and reprioritise WMS tasks for put-away to Zone B, E and the hazmat cage in Zone F, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C, picking, packing and staging in Zone D, and you confirm that main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack aisles of 3.0 m and dock approaches are clear before work begins.

4. You enforce safety standards continuously. You ensure everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear, seat belts are worn whenever a truck is moving, and the three speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are obeyed. You ensure pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

5. You are the incident lead on your shift. Every injury, near miss, damage to racking including any defect affecting the 2,700 kg bay limit in Zone B, breach of the 1,000 kg pallet limit, temperature alarm in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, and spill in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F with its 4,000 kg limit is reported to you immediately. You secure and barrier the area, arrange first aid, and initiate response under PR-09, PR-13 and PR-14.

6. You review every incident report arising on your shift before it closes. You check facts with witnesses, confirm quarantine moves to Zone F the same day, bay blocks in the WMS, truck tag-outs and notifications to the maintenance technician and dispatcher, and you decide corrective action. No blocked bay, tagged truck or cage access returns to service without required inspection and log.

7. You approve decisions on the floor within fixed thresholds only. You approve damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR after same-day quarantine in Zone F under PR-09, and you approve the final disposition of all inspected returns in Zone F as restock, rework or scrap under PR-07. Write-offs above 500 EUR are escalated to the warehouse manager.

8. You control temporary changes on the floor. You authorise any short-notice obstruction, closure of an aisle, walkway or dock approach, and you inform the dispatcher immediately so door and time-slot assignments for doors 1 to 8 at 1.2 m height can be adjusted. You do not change dock designations, zone boundaries or site limits without warehouse manager approval.

9. You coordinate continuously with the dispatcher who owns dock scheduling. The dispatcher decides which carrier gets which door and time slot — doors 1-4 inbound only, doors 5-8 outbound only — and releases every outbound load from Zone D. You decide how the floor prepares, stages and executes that plan safely, and you do not load or unload without dispatcher confirmation.

10. You own handover under PR-15. At 14:00 you conduct a face-to-face handover on the floor with the incoming supervisor covering dock status, vehicles in the marked waiting area, open WMS tasks for the 20 scanners, goods in Zone A awaiting check, pick faces in Zone C, staged loads in Zone D, manual verification in Zone E, quarantine and hazmat quantities in Zone F, and all open incidents and defects. At 22:00 you close the site and record overnight status for 06:00. You remain accountable until handover is signed.

11. You escalate to the warehouse manager before action where doubt arises on authority, where a defect affects capacity or safety, or where overtime or forklift authorisation is requested. You record all approvals with name, date and value and you never delegate your thresholds.

title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
text:
1. You are the dispatcher and you own dock scheduling for the whole Harborwick site. You book all transport, assign every carrier a specific door and time slot, and release every outbound load. No vehicle approaches, unloads or loads without your confirmed assignment and, for outbound, your release.

2. You book both inbound and outbound carriers against demand and cut-off. You agree the booking reference, carrier identity, load type and quantity, and you confirm the door and slot in advance. You suspend or re-plan bookings for the annual wall-to-wall stocktake shutdown and for any closure directed by the warehouse manager.

3. You assign doors strictly by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading in Zone A. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading from Zone D. You never assign inbound to doors 5 to 8 or outbound to doors 1 to 4, and you do not change a designation without prior approval by the warehouse manager.

4. Every assignment records door number at 1.2 m dock height, date, time slot and carrier, and is communicated to the gate and to the shift supervisor. You are the only person who makes or changes an assignment. No change is made on the floor without your confirmation.

5. You control the arrival flow through the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. Drivers report to the gate or to you and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area. You call each vehicle forward only at its assigned time when the door is free and Zone A or Zone D is ready as confirmed by the shift supervisor.

6. You work to fixed site limits. You do not book or assign any delivery that would require a pallet above 1,000 kg including load, that would exceed the 2,700 kg rack bay limit in Zone B when put away, or that would take the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F above 4,000 kg. Where a booking would breach a limit you hold it in the vehicle or in Zone A and refer to the shift supervisor for partial acceptance or refusal.

7. You release every outbound load from Zone D under PR-06. You release only when the load is fully wrapped on the 2 stretch wrappers, labelled with a WMS-generated label, closed in the WMS and physically staged by door and load in the 900 m2 Zone D lanes. No unwrapped, unlabelled or unreleased pallet is released, and no loading at doors 5 to 8 begins without your release.

8. You apply vehicle capacity rules on every release. The curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets; payload weight governs. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions and takes at most one full-weight pallet. Any consignment above 1,200 kg or requiring more than one full-weight pallet is assigned to trailer only.

9. You plan outbound throughput within the site maximum. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved only by the warehouse manager. This equals 12 trailer loads or 288 full-weight pallets per shift. You do not promise a client more than 288 full-weight pallets in one shift.

10. You coordinate continuously with the shift supervisor who runs the floor. You decide which door and when; the supervisor decides how the floor prepares, stages and executes safely in Zones A to D, keeping 4.0 m main transport aisles and 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers clear. If floor readiness conflicts with the dock plan, you decide the door plan and the supervisor decides the safe method.

11. You maintain the door board, waiting-area list and load manifest with carrier, door, slot, pallet count, total weight and release status, and you record every release with load reference, date, time and your name. You inform the supervisor immediately of delays, early or late arrivals, incomplete loads and any door or leveller fault, and you re-assign slots to keep dock approaches and yard lanes clear.

12. You enforce driver discipline. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment or dock levellers and never open a dock door. Dock levellers at all eight doors are operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently assigned. You escalate any breach, any request to change site limits or any doubt on authority to the warehouse manager before action, and you include open assignments, waiting vehicles and release status in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
text:
1. You are one of the eight forklift operators. You operate materials handling equipment to move, put away, replenish and load pallets in Zones A to F on WMS tasks. You do not pick orders, book receipts or inspect returns — you execute only system-directed truck tasks.

2. You drive only when personally authorised in writing by the warehouse manager after licence, training and site assessment under PR-10. No licence, no truck. Your authorisation is specific to truck type — 2.5 t counterbalance or 1.6 t reach truck — and is posted on the authorised list. You check the list at the start of every shift.

3. You operate the electric fleet only: the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work and dock work at the eight 1.2 m doors, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, and the 8 electric pallet jacks for horizontal moves. You do not operate any other truck type. Hand pallet jacks are for small manual moves at walking pace only.

4. You work only on a released WMS task on one of the 20 handheld scanners. You scan the pallet licence plate and the source and destination locations to open and close each move. No hand-written location, verbal instruction or unlabelled pallet replaces the scanner task. A rejected scan is not forced — you stop and report to the shift supervisor.

5. You obey the three speed limits on every move without exception: 10 km/h inside the building in the 6,000 m2 hall, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard, and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps, whether pedestrians are present or not. Limits apply laden and unladen, forward and reverse.

6. You stay on vehicle routes only. You travel on the 4.0 m main transport aisles between Zones A to F and to and from doors 1 to 8. You enter the 3.0 m rack aisles in Zone B only when your WMS task requires put-away or retrieval there. You never enter the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers, and you never walk a load through a pedestrian crossing except at the marked crossing at 5 km/h.

7. You wear high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times on the floor, and you wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning on levellers at doors 1 to 8. No passengers are carried and no truck moves with the seat belt unfastened.

8. You observe the site pallet limit on every lift: every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. You do not lift, move to height or load to a vehicle any pallet indicating overweight, instability, collapse or unsafe wrapping. You hold it in place and report to the shift supervisor for quarantine to Zone F the same day under PR-09.

9. You observe the bay and stacking limits. In Zone B you put away only to a vacant position within the 2,700 kg rack bay limit — at 1,000 kg this means at most 2 full-weight pallets per bay — and the WMS will block any excess. Where block stacking outside racking is directed, you stack at most 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high, only in designated areas, never in rack aisles or against uprights.

10. You handle cold and hazmat only on directed tasks. You move pallets to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C only when booked with cold-chain status directly to a vacant chilled location, and to the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F only when quantity has been checked against the 4,000 kg cage limit — at most 4 full-weight pallets — with the WMS blocking any excess. No hazmat goes to any other zone.

11. You carry out a documented pre-use check on your assigned truck before its first use each day under PR-10, using the daily check sheet for that truck type. You check tyres, forks, carriage, chains, mast, brakes, steering, lights, horn, reversing alarm, seat belt, overhead guard, battery and emergency stop, and you record truck ID, date, time, name and signature for countersignature by the shift supervisor.

12. A truck that has not passed its daily check is not used for any move, and any defect arising during the shift is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. You tag the truck out, remove the keys and apply the do-not-use notice, and you do not return it to service until the maintenance technician has logged the repair and, for any defect affecting capacity, braking, steering or the 1,000 kg and 2,700 kg limits, the warehouse manager has approved return.

13. You keep aisles, dock approaches and walkways clear, you stop immediately for any incident, near miss or barrier damage and report to the shift supervisor, and you include open tasks, defects and exceptions in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

title: 2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
text:
1. You are one of the six inbound operators. You work only in Zone A at inbound doors 1 to 4. You receive, count and inspect all inbound goods in the 800 m2 receiving area before anything is booked or put away. No goods move past Zone A on your shift without your checks.

2. You work only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager, and only under the shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. You take task direction from the supervisor and door and time-slot assignments from the dispatcher.

3. You apply the document-first rule under PR-01 without exception. Before any pallet is removed from the vehicle, you check paperwork at the document-check area inside doors 1 to 4: carrier identity, booking reference, door 1 to 4 and time-slot assignment, purchase order, supplier, pallet count, product description and seal number where applicable.

4. You do not unload until the check is complete and accepted. The vehicle must be correctly positioned at its assigned 1.2 m door, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller deployed by trained staff. You confirm accepted on the paperwork with date, time, door, name and signature. Only then is unloading released.

5. If documents are missing, do not match the booking, refer to unscheduled goods, or indicate an overage that would breach the 1,000 kg pallet limit or the 4,000 kg limit for the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, you hold the delivery in the vehicle or in the holding location in Zone A. You escalate immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher and make no booking.

6. You unload and stage for count in Zone A with forklift operator support for palletised loads. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 yard, never enter Zone A and never operate equipment. You observe speed limits of 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and you use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

7. You count every pallet and unit by purchase order against the checked documents and record door, date, time and checker name. At the same time you inspect each pallet for damage, wet packaging, leakage, seal integrity, labelling, expiry and temperature condition for chilled goods. You hold any pallet indicating overweight, instability or unsafe wrapping and report it to the supervisor.

8. You identify hazardous materials during inspection and check quantity against the 4,000 kg cage limit before acceptance. No quantity above that limit is booked. You segregate damaged goods immediately, record quantity and reason, and ensure they are booked to quarantine status and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are never counted as available stock.

9. You book only inspected goods. Using one of the 20 handheld scanners under PR-01, you create the WMS receipt against the booking reference, recording SKU, quantity, pallet identity, expiry and weight for the 1,000 kg check. On successful booking you apply the system-generated pallet licence plate and ensure it is scannable. Pallets without a label are not released.

10. You release to put-away only when three confirmations are met in Zone A: documents checked and signed, count and inspection recorded, and WMS booking completed with label applied. Forklift operators then execute put-away to Zone B to a vacant position within the 2,700 kg bay limit and 2,400 positions, to Zone E directly to a chilled location between +2 °C and +8 °C, or to the hazmat cage in Zone F within the 4,000 kg limit, only against a released WMS task.

11. You keep Zone A lanes, inspection benches and dock approaches clear for their full width at all times. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m are kept clear and no storage takes place outside marked Zone A locations. You report any scanner fault, label failure, location block or discrepancy to the shift supervisor and hold the pallet in Zone A until corrected.

12. You wear high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times on the floor. You report every shortage, overage, damage, quarantine move and refused delivery to the supervisor for PR-15 handover, and you notify the dispatcher when doors 1 to 4 are free for the next assigned slot.

title: 2.3 Picker - Replenishment, Picking and Handover to Dispatch
text:
1. You are one of the ten pickers. You work only in Zone C in the 1,200 m2 picking area on ground-level pick faces and flow racks. You pick customer orders against WMS scanner tasks and hand verified pallets to Zone D for dispatch. You do not receive in Zone A, put away to high bays in Zone B, or operate counterbalance forklifts or reach trucks.

2. You work only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager, and only under the shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. Floaters covering picking work only as pickers on your tasks.

3. You never pick from an empty or unreplenished face. Zone C holds no bulk reserve and no quarantine or hazmat. All pick faces are fed from bulk storage in Zone B under PR-03 before your picking shift. You start a wave only after the shift supervisor has confirmed replenishment complete and released Zone C to picking.

4. You work scanner-driven on one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners under PR-04. The WMS directs your wave, sequence, aisle and face. You log on, confirm the wave and follow face-by-face order. Flow racks are picked from the front pick side only; you never access the rear replenishment side. No paper list, verbal instruction or memory pick replaces the scanner task.

5. You scan-verify every item before it is packed. At each face you scan the pick-face location label, then scan each SKU, batch and quantity as directed. The system verifies location, SKU, batch, expiry and quantity. You do not proceed to the next face until the scan is accepted. Only scan-verified lines are authorised for packing under PR-05.

6. You never force a scan. Wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong quantity, expired or unreadable barcode stops the pick at that face. You leave the stock in place, record scan-failed or short on the scanner and report immediately to the shift supervisor. The supervisor decides on face check, recount by the stock controller, or replenishment from Zone B. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

7. You segregate suspect stock immediately. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found at the face are not picked and not verified. You report to the supervisor and ensure they are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The pallet or location is left empty and you record the exception in the WMS.

8. You record short picks accurately. Where the face quantity is insufficient you enter the actual quantity picked and confirm short pick on the scanner. The WMS logs the shortage for the supervisor to trigger replenishment. You do not over-pick from another face to make up the quantity.

9. You keep each order pallet stable, within the pallet footprint and under the site limit of 1,000 kg including load. You use only the 12 hand pallet jacks and 8 electric pallet jacks for small moves in Zone C at walking pace and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones. Counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are for authorised forklift operators only.

10. On completion of a wave you present the pallet at the Zone C to Zone D handover point, close the WMS task and ensure the pallet label is scannable. Only closed, scan-verified and packed pallets move to Zone D. Unwrapped, unlabelled or unverified pallets remain in Zone C. Wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and staging by door and load in the 900 m2 Zone D is carried out under PR-05 and PR-06 and loading at doors 5 to 8 is only on dispatcher release.

11. You observe pedestrian and speed rules at all times. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory in Zone C. You use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and marked crossings, never walk in the 4.0 m main transport aisles or 3.0 m rack aisles except at crossings, and obey 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

12. You report every scan failure, short pick, quarantine move, scanner fault or face shortage to the shift supervisor during the shift. You keep Zone C faces, flow lanes and handover points clear and include open picks, exceptions and faults for PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.1 Stock Controller - Inventory Accuracy and Cycle Counts
text:
1. You are one of the two stock controllers. You own inventory accuracy day to day for the whole site — Zones A to F. You ensure the stock in the system is the stock on the rack. You do not receive in Zone A, pick in Zone C or inspect returns in Zone F except through the count process.

2. You work only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager, and under the shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. You work on WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners under PR-08.

3. You plan and execute cycle counts every working day Monday to Friday on the rotating zone schedule. The schedule covers Zone A 800 m2, Zone B 2,200 m2 with 2,400 high-bay positions, Zone C 1,200 m2, Zone D 900 m2, Zone E 300 m2 and Zone F 600 m2 including the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. High-movement areas in Zone B and Zone C are counted more frequently.

4. You generate counts system-directed and blind. You issue WMS tasks by location only with no display of system quantity. The counter scans the location label in the zone and enters the counted quantity by pallet, case, SKU, batch and expiry where applicable. No paper count or pre-printed quantity replaces the scanner task.

5. At the start of each shift you confirm with the shift supervisor that 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles are clear and that counting will not obstruct replenishment from Zone B to Zone C, picking or dock activity at the 1.2 m doors. You carry out counts at walking pace and obey 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

6. You apply the second-count rule without exception. No inventory adjustment is posted without a second count. Where a first count does not match the system, the WMS generates a second-count task for the same location on a different scanner to a different person. The first counter never recounts their own location.

7. You carry out second counts yourself. The second count is by the second stock controller or, where both are engaged, by the shift supervisor acting as second counter. You record counter name, date, time and location blind. Where first and second counts agree the variance is confirmed; where they disagree you escalate to the shift supervisor for a third count and investigation.

8. You treat damaged stock as unavailable. Damaged, wet, leaking or suspect stock found during a count is not counted as available, is reported to the shift supervisor and is moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. You do not adjust it on the spot and the location remains blocked pending inspection.

9. You count Zone E and the hazmat cage in place. In Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C you coordinate short planned openings with the supervisor, doors closed between locations, monitoring and alarms active. In the 60 m2 hazmat cage you count against the 4,000 kg limit — at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets — and no pallet is removed from the cage for counting.

10. You prepare adjustments only after second-count evidence. You enter reason, location, SKU, quantity, both counter names and references for the shift supervisor to review. Adjustments arising from daily cycle counts are approved only by the shift supervisor. You do not post until that approval with name, date and time is recorded in the WMS.

11. You lead the annual wall-to-wall stocktake under the warehouse manager under PR-08. You support the shutdown of all receiving at doors 1 to 4, put-away, replenishment, picking and loading at doors 5 to 8, the WMS freeze at cut-off, blind location-by-location counting of every pallet on site and second counts for every discrepancy. Only the warehouse manager signs off the stocktake results and any adjustment from it; you post only after that written sign-off.

12. You keep the audit trail complete. You retain all first counts, second counts, variances, blocked bays including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, quarantine quantities and approvals, and you include open variances and pending approvals in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.2 Returns and Packing Staff - Returns Inspection and Packing
text:
1. You are one of the four returns and packing staff. You work only in Zone F in the 600 m2 services and control area, in the returns inspection area, the quarantine area and the value-added packing area. You inspect every return, propose disposition and carry out packing tasks on WMS direction. You do not receive in Zone A, pick in Zone C or count as stock controller.

2. You work only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager, and only under the shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. You work on tasks issued to the 20 handheld scanners under PR-07 and PR-09.

3. You handle returns only in Zone F. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 calendar days of the original delivery date only, from the outbound manifest. Returns arrive at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4 at a time slot agreed with the dispatcher, are checked for eligibility in Zone A and are moved directly to you in Zone F booked to returns status.

4. You check eligibility before inspection: customer name, original order and load reference, delivery date, return date, SKU, quantity and reason. Where the delivery was more than 14 days ago, cannot be matched or would breach the 1,000 kg pallet limit or the 4,000 kg limit for the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, you do not inspect. You escalate to the shift supervisor for refusal at the door.

5. You inspect every unit individually at the bench in Zone F. No bulk acceptance or sample check replaces unit-by-unit inspection. You record against the checklist: outer packaging, inner seal integrity, labelling and batch or expiry, leakage, wetting, contamination, odour, temperature condition for Zone E goods between +2 °C and +8 °C, and evidence of use or tampering, with your name, date and time.

6. You segregate damaged goods immediately. Damaged, leaking, wet, open, out-of-temperature or suspect goods found during inspection are not held in the returns lanes. You book them to quarantine status in the WMS, label them as quarantine and move them to the physically separated quarantine area in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are not available for picking or dispatch.

7. You handle hazardous returns only under PR-13. Hazmat is stored only inside the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, total quantity never above 4,000 kg — at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets — with incompatible classes segregated. You count it against the limit and leave the cage locked except on a released WMS task.

8. On completion of inspection you propose disposition in the WMS for each quantity: restock to available stock, rework in Zone F, or scrap for disposal, with condition, quantity for each route and reason. No goods are restocked, reworked or scrapped without your proposal recorded.

9. You do not decide final disposition. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of every inspected return as restock, rework or scrap under PR-07, and approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR; above 500 EUR the warehouse manager approves. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

10. You execute only approved moves from Zone F. Restock is moved on a released WMS task to a directed location in Zone B within the 2,700 kg bay limit, Zone E or pick faces; rework remains in the value-added packing area clearly marked as rework until reinspected and re-approved; scrap is booked to scrap, marked and held in quarantine pending disposal.

11. You carry out value-added packing in Zone F as directed by WMS tasks and the shift supervisor. You pack stable and within the pallet footprint under the 1,000 kg limit, use approved materials and keep packing benches and lanes clear. You do not pack damaged or quarantined stock unless directed as approved rework.

12. You wear high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times in Zone F, with additional SDS PPE in the hazmat cage. You obey 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and the Zone F access, and you use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers, keeping 4.0 m main transport aisles and cage approaches clear.

13. You report every inspection result, quarantine transfer, hazmat quantity and packing completion to the shift supervisor during the shift, retain the returns receipt, 14-day check and inspection record in the WMS, and include open returns, quarantine quantities and pending dispositions in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance
text:
1. You are the maintenance technician. You maintain all materials handling equipment, racking and dock equipment for the whole Harborwick site — the 6,000 m2 hall, the 3,500 m2 fenced yard and Zones A to F. You are the only person who carries out planned maintenance, inspections and repairs, and you log every job.

2. You work only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager, under the shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. You do not approve overtime, authorise forklift operators or change site limits.

3. You maintain the all-electric MHE fleet to manufacturer schedules under PR-10: the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, the 8 electric pallet jacks, the 12 hand pallet jacks pushed at walking pace, plus the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D, the 1 cardboard baler and the 20 handheld WMS scanners. Charging is from the designated area only.

4. You carry out the documented safety inspection of high-bay pallet racking in Zone B every month. You inspect all 2,400 positions in the 2,200 m2 bulk area bay by bay — uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings, beam connectors and load signs — against the 2,700 kg bay limit, and designated block-stack areas against the 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high limits. You record pass, monitor or block for each bay with location, date, photographs and name.

5. You maintain all eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height and their levellers. You inspect structure, lip, controls and interlocks, maintain the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers for clear width, markings and signs, and you check pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps where the 5 km/h limit applies.

6. You maintain the specialist systems. For Zone E of 300 m2 you service the refrigeration plant, doors, seals, continuous monitoring and audible alarms for +2 °C to +8 °C and support the manual verification each shift. For the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F you service forced ventilation, spill containment, signage and the spill kit at the cage entrance, and you enforce the 4,000 kg cage limit — at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets.

7. You inspect, repair and replace fixed yellow barriers, floor markings, overhead signage, lighting and emergency exit hardware as part of the monthly inspection. You keep walkways at 1.2 m, main aisles at 4.0 m and rack aisles at 3.0 m clear and fully signed, and you barrier off any damaged barrier or route until repaired.

8. You log every inspection and every repair in the maintenance record under PR-10. Each entry records date, time, equipment or bay ID, zone, defect found, action taken, parts used, your name and operator name, downtime and, where capacity or safety is affected, the warehouse manager approval for return to service. Daily check sheets, monthly racking sheets and repair logs are kept together for audit.

9. You respond immediately to defects reported by operators or the shift supervisor. You tag out any truck, wrapper, baler, leveller, rack bay or barrier that is unsafe — keys removed, do-not-use notice applied — and you block the bay or location in the WMS. Defects affecting braking, steering, forks, chains, seat belts, barriers, levellers, the 1,000 kg pallet limit, the 2,700 kg bay limit or the 4,000 kg hazmat limit are escalated to the shift supervisor and are not returned to service until repaired, re-inspected and approved by the warehouse manager.

10. You support the daily pre-use checks under PR-10. You provide correct check sheets for each truck type, advise operators on faults, and you verify and countersign repairs before the shift supervisor countersigns the serviceable record. You do not carry out the operator's check for them.

11. You support emergency preparedness under PR-12, PR-13 and PR-14. You test evacuation alarms throughout the hall and yard to schedule, maintain emergency lighting and routes to the assembly point by the north fence, and you attend the evacuation drill every quarter and any cold-chain or hazmat incident to verify refrigeration, ventilation and alarms before the warehouse manager clears the area for re-entry.

12. You keep the site plan, WMS location master and posted rack and cage signs aligned. You make no change to rack layout, bay capacity, stacking areas, aisle widths, barrier positions, cage location or size, leveller controls, fleet numbers or ratings until prior approval by the warehouse manager is given and the updated plan and WMS locations are in place.

13. You work safely at all times in high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear, with additional SDS PPE in the hazmat cage and insulated clothing for Zone E, you obey 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, you escalate any doubt on authority to the shift supervisor before action, and you include open defects, blocked bays, tagged equipment and pending approvals in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
text:
1. You work only within the rostered site hours Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. There is no routine weekend working; Saturday morning overtime in peak season takes place only when approved in advance by the warehouse manager. No shift operates without its shift supervisor present and in charge of the floor.

2. You attend for your assigned shift and remain on the floor or in your zone until relieved or released by the shift supervisor. You do not extend a shift, start early or remain outside your rostered period unless directed for a specific operational or safety reason. Attendance and absence are managed by the shift supervisor, with the two floaters deployed to cover absence.

3. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in the 6,000 m2 hall in Zones A to F, at the dock levellers and on all walkways, without exception. No person steps onto the warehouse floor without both items correctly worn and fastened. Forklift and reach truck operators wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.

4. You obey the three speed limits on every shift: 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard, and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps, whether pedestrians are present or not. Limits apply to all powered equipment and to all visiting vehicles.

5. You use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers as pedestrian routes. You keep the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles clear for their full width, cross only at marked crossings, and never walk behind a vehicle at a dock or across a leveller unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

6. You respect zone discipline and flow. Zone A 800 m2 is receiving, Zone B 2,200 m2 is bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C 1,200 m2 is picking, Zone D 900 m2 is dispatch, Zone E 300 m2 is chilled storage and Zone F 600 m2 is services, quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No storage takes place outside marked zones and locations.

7. You observe load and capacity limits on every task. Every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg; each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg; block stacking outside racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high; total quantity in the hazmat cage never exceeds 4,000 kg. You do not lift, store or load any pallet above 1,000 kg.

8. You follow dock discipline. Doors 1 to 4 at 1.2 m height are inbound only, doors 5 to 8 are outbound only. Every carrier is assigned a door and time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area, never enter the hall and never operate equipment or levellers.

9. You maintain cold-chain and hazmat awareness. Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C with continuous monitoring, audible alarms and manual verification each shift. The hazmat cage is locked, ventilated and subject to the 4,000 kg limit. You report any alarm, excursion, door fault, leak or spill immediately to the shift supervisor and do not move affected stock until cleared.

10. You operate equipment only when authorised. No person drives the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t or the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t without personal written authorisation from the warehouse manager after licence, training and site assessment. No licence, no truck. Every powered truck receives a documented pre-use check before first use each day under PR-10.

11. You follow the fifteen mandatory procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and role boundaries. You carry out only the duties of your assigned role under WMS direction, you do not post any inventory adjustment without a second count, and you accept that approvals are fixed: overtime and authorisations only by the warehouse manager, dock scheduling and load release only by the dispatcher, write-offs and return dispositions by threshold to the shift supervisor.

12. You report every incident immediately to the shift supervisor — injury, near miss, rack or equipment damage, speed breach, temperature alarm or hazmat spill — and you stop work at that location until the supervisor attends. You cooperate with PR-14 evacuation to the assembly point by the north fence, complete roll call before any re-entry, and attend quarterly drills and briefings as directed.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
text:
1. Harborwick provides inbound receiving at doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 only. Doors 1 to 4 are inbound only at 1.2 m dock height with dock leveller. No inbound unloading is offered at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Standard receiving windows are Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, aligned to the two rostered shifts. All unloading, counting, inspection and system booking in Zone A takes place within these windows.

3. No routine weekend receiving is included. Saturday morning overtime in peak season is available only when approved in advance by the warehouse manager and is limited to the morning period.

4. Every inbound delivery is by prior booking. The dispatcher assigns each carrier a specific inbound door and time slot before arrival and confirms the booking reference. Harborwick will receive only carriers with a confirmed door and slot assignment.

5. Carriers must report arrival to the gate or dispatcher and wait with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers do not enter the hall and do not approach a door until called forward at the assigned time. Vehicles arriving early or outside slot will be rescheduled to the next available inbound slot.

6. Harborwick commits to the document-to-booking sequence without exception. No pallet is removed from the vehicle until document check in Zone A is complete. The check verifies carrier identity, booking reference, door and slot, purchase order or inbound reference, supplier and declared pallet quantity.

7. If documents are missing, do not match the booking, or refer to unscheduled goods, unloading will be held and the client and carrier notified via the dispatcher. No goods move beyond Zone A and no booking is made until the discrepancy is resolved.

8. After accepted document check, Harborwick will unload, count and inspect in Zone A. Count is by purchase order against checked documents; inspection covers damage, wet packaging, leakage, seal and labelling integrity and, for chilled goods, temperature condition and expiry where applicable.

9. Only inspected goods in Zone A are booked into the WMS, and only booked goods are released for physical put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Uninspected goods remain in Zone A and will not be put away or made available for order fulfilment.

10. On successful booking Harborwick creates the WMS receipt and applies a scannable pallet licence plate for each accepted pallet. The receipt records SKU, quantity, pallet identity, expiry where applicable and pallet weight against the site limit of 1,000 kg per pallet including load. Pallets without a WMS licence plate are not released.

11. Goods requiring hazardous storage are checked at inspection against the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F. Harborwick will not book or store quantity that would exceed that limit. Excess will be held in Zone A or in the vehicle for client decision on partial acceptance or refusal.

12. Harborwick will confirm completion of receiving by door, with date, time, accepted quantity and exceptions noted on the paperwork and in the WMS. Shortages, overages and damaged quantities are recorded at that point and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day where applicable.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
text:
1. Harborwick provides outbound dispatch at doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 only. Doors 5 to 8 are outbound only at 1.2 m dock height with dock leveller. No outbound loading is offered at inbound doors 1 to 4.

2. Standard dispatch windows are Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, aligned to the two rostered shifts. All packing, wrapping, staging in Zone D and loading takes place within these windows.

3. No routine weekend dispatch is included. Saturday morning overtime in peak season is available only when approved in advance by the warehouse manager and is limited to the morning period. No Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday dispatch is offered.

4. Every outbound load is by prior booking. The dispatcher assigns each carrier a specific outbound door and time slot before arrival and confirms the door, slot and load reference. Harborwick will load only carriers with a confirmed door and slot assignment and a released load.

5. Carriers must report arrival to the gate or dispatcher and wait with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the fenced yard. Drivers do not enter the hall, do not operate materials handling equipment or dock levellers, and do not approach a door until called forward at the assigned time.

6. Harborwick commits that only verified pallets are staged for dispatch. Every item picked in Zone C is scan-verified on a handheld WMS scanner — location, SKU, batch and quantity — before it is authorised for packing. No unverified, unlabelled or unwrapped pallet is placed in Zone D.

7. Packing, labelling and wrapping are completed in Zone D before staging. Each pallet is placed stable within the pallet footprint, labelled with a WMS-generated scannable label showing customer, order and destination, and wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers with the label visible and scannable after wrapping. Hand-written labels are not used.

8. Only wrapped, labelled and system-closed pallets are eligible for staging. Staging takes place solely in Zone D of 900 m², by outbound door and by load and drop sequence as shown on the WMS outbound manifest. No staging takes place outside Zone D.

9. Every outbound pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Harborwick will not wrap, stage or load any pallet above 1,000 kg. Overweight, unstable, leaking or damaged pallets are segregated in Zone D, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day and excluded from the load.

10. No loading begins without dispatcher release. Release is given only when the complete load is wrapped, labelled, closed in the WMS and physically staged in its correct lane in Zone D, and the assigned vehicle is confirmed for that door and slot.

11. Loading at doors 5 to 8 begins only when the vehicle is correctly positioned, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller safely deployed by trained warehouse staff. Each pallet is scanned by licence plate against the released load. Any quantity, label or destination mismatch stops loading for client and dispatcher resolution.

12. Harborwick plans outbound throughput on fixed vehicle and door capacities. The contracted curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets; the delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions and takes at most one full-weight pallet. Consignments above 1,200 kg are assigned to trailer only.

13. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer this equates to a site maximum of 12 trailer loads or 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. Harborwick will not promise a client more than 288 full-weight pallets in a single shift.

14. On completion of loading Harborwick closes the load in the WMS, seals the vehicle and completes dispatch paperwork with door, carrier, load reference, pallet count, total weight, date, time and loader and dispatcher names. No vehicle is released from the yard without completed paperwork and dispatcher confirmation.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
text:
1. Harborwick operates eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller, on the yard side of the 6,000 m² hall within the 3,500 m² fenced yard. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading. No door is used for the opposite flow for any client or carrier.

2. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot, sequences loads by cut-off and carrier booking, and releases every outbound load from Zone D. No other role makes or changes a door or slot assignment.

3. Every inbound and outbound movement is by prior booking with a confirmed assignment before arrival. The assignment records door number, date, time slot, carrier and booking or load reference and is communicated to the gate and the shift supervisor. Harborwick will not receive or load a vehicle without a confirmed assignment for that door and slot.

4. No vehicle approaches a door without instruction. On arrival carriers report to the gate or dispatcher and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers do not enter the hall, do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to the door only at the assigned time when called forward.

5. A vehicle that arrives early, late or without a booking waits only in the marked waiting area and is rescheduled to the next available slot for that flow by the dispatcher. Vehicles do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes while waiting. The dispatcher informs the shift supervisor of any delay, rescheduling or door closure immediately.

6. Door changes, time-slot changes and re-bookings are made only by the dispatcher. Floor staff do not reassign doors. Where Zone A or Zone D is not ready, the shift supervisor advises the dispatcher, who decides the revised door plan while the supervisor decides the safe method of work on the floor.

7. Harborwick applies a fixed site pallet limit to all transport planning. Every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Harborwick will not accept, book, stage or load any pallet above 1,000 kg. Any pallet presented above that limit is held for client decision and excluded from throughput calculations.

8. Vehicle capacities offered to clients are fixed and governed by weight before floor space. The contracted curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. Where pallets weigh less than 1,000 kg, additional pallets may be loaded to use floor space provided the 24,000 kg payload is not exceeded and the load is stable.

9. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg payload on 6 floor positions and takes at most one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet. No van is loaded beyond 1,200 kg. Any consignment exceeding 1,200 kg or requiring more than one full-weight pallet is assigned to trailer and loaded only at doors 5 to 8.

10. Hazardous consignments are planned within the same scheduling system and against the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F, meaning at most 4 full-weight pallets in the cage at any time. Harborwick will not schedule or accept inbound hazmat that would exceed that limit.

11. Promised outbound throughput is fixed by doors and turn rate. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. This equates to 12 trailer loads per shift.

12. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, the site maximum is 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. This is the most Harborwick will promise a single client or a group of clients for one shift. Client orders exceeding that volume will be scheduled across consecutive shifts or days by the dispatcher in agreement with the client.

13. Any change to door designations, time-slot arrangements, vehicle ratings or the 288-pallet shift maximum requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and advance notice to clients before it is offered as a service level.

title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
text:
1. Harborwick provides order picking only from Zone C of 1,200 m², comprising ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone C holds no bulk reserve, no quarantine stock and no hazardous materials. All pick faces in Zone C are fed exclusively by replenishment from bulk storage in Zone B.

2. Replenishment of pick faces is carried out under PR-03 before each picking shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. Harborwick commits that no picking wave starts until the shift supervisor has confirmed replenishment complete and Zone C released for picking.

3. Replenishment is system-directed via the WMS. Tasks are generated from current pick-face levels, open customer orders and available booked stock in Zone B, and are executed by authorised forklift operators on handheld scanners against the 2,400 bulk positions and the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg.

4. Picking is carried out under PR-04 on scanner-directed tasks only. Ten pickers work in Zone C on the 20 handheld WMS scanners, following the WMS wave, sequence and face. Flow racks are picked from the front pick side only. No paper picks, verbal instructions or memory picks are used.

5. Harborwick commits to 100% scan verification of every picked item before packing. At each face the picker scans the pick-face location label and then scans each SKU, batch, expiry where applicable, and quantity as directed. The WMS verifies all three before authorising packing.

6. A pick is accepted only where location matches task, SKU and batch match order, and quantity matches directed quantity. The WMS closes the pick line only on that three-way match. No forced confirmation or manual override is permitted on the scanner.

7. Any scan failure stops the pick at that face. Wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong expiry, wrong quantity or unreadable barcode is recorded as scan-failed on the scanner, stock is left in place and the shift supervisor is notified immediately for face check, recount by the stock controller or re-directed replenishment.

8. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found at the face are not picked and not verified. They are segregated, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09, with the exception recorded in the WMS.

9. Where the face quantity is insufficient, the picker records the actual quantity picked and confirms short pick on the scanner. Harborwick logs the shortage as a verified short pick, retains the order line as incomplete and triggers replenishment from Zone B. No substitution from another face is made without a new WMS task.

10. Only scan-verified lines are authorised for packing and labelling. Packing under PR-05 begins only after WMS authorisation for that order or pallet. Goods are placed stable within the pallet footprint under the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load.

11. Labelling accuracy is WMS-controlled. Labels are applied only to scan-verified and packed pallets in Zone D, after scanning the pallet licence plate and applying the WMS-generated label showing customer, order and destination. Hand-written or non-matching labels are not used.

12. On completion of a wave, Harborwick closes the verified pallet in the WMS as ready for Zone D, recording picker name, scanner ID, date and time and linking the pallet to its order and outbound load. Only closed, scan-verified pallets are transferred to dispatch staging in Zone D.

13. All scan verifications, failures, short picks, quarantine moves and packing completions are recorded automatically in the WMS. Harborwick makes the verification record available to the client on request and reviews exceptions during the shift for correction before dispatch.

14. Any scanner fault, label misprint or system rejection that prevents verification holds the affected pallet in Zone C. Harborwick will not move the pallet to Zone D, wrap or load it until the fault is corrected and successful scan verification is completed on a serviceable scanner.

title: 2.2 Stock Counts, Reconciliations and Adjustments
text:
1. Harborwick operates cycle counting under PR-08 every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule across Zones A to F. The schedule covers Zone A 800 m², Zone B 2,200 m² with 2,400 high-bay positions, Zone C 1,200 m², Zone D 900 m², Zone E 300 m² and Zone F 600 m² including the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage. High-movement areas in Zone B and Zone C are counted more frequently.

2. Cycle counts are planned and executed by the two stock controllers. Harborwick will issue WMS tasks to the 20 handheld scanners and will not delegate count planning or adjustment preparation to any other role.

3. All cycle counts are system-directed and blind. The WMS selects locations and SKUs for the day and generates tasks showing location only. System quantity is not displayed to the counter until the count is entered.

4. Counts are carried out only within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. Harborwick will coordinate counting in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C to minimise door open time, with doors closed between locations and continuous monitoring and alarms active.

5. Harborwick commits to the recount rule without exception: no inventory adjustment is posted without a second count. Where a first count entered on the scanner does not match system quantity, the WMS automatically generates a second-count task for the same location to a different person on a different scanner.

6. The second count is carried out blind by the second stock controller or, where both are engaged, by the shift supervisor acting as second counter. The first counter does not recount their own location. Results are recorded with counter name, date, time and location.
