7. Where first and second counts agree, Harborwick confirms the variance against the system and prepares the adjustment. Where they disagree, no adjustment is prepared; the shift supervisor checks the location for recent put-away, replenishment or quarantine moves and orders a third count to determine the verified quantity.

8. Damaged, wet, leaking or suspect stock found during any count is not counted as available. Harborwick will segregate it in place, report it to the shift supervisor and move it to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The location remains blocked pending inspection.

9. Counts in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage are carried out in place against the cage limit of 4,000 kg, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. No chilled or hazardous pallet is removed from its location for counting.

10. Adjustments arising from daily cycle counts are prepared by the stock controllers with reason, location, SKU, quantity and both counter names, and are approved only by the shift supervisor. Harborwick will not post the adjustment until that approval with name, date and time is recorded in the WMS.

11. Harborwick carries out a full wall-to-wall stocktake once per calendar year under PR-08. The site is shut down for the count: no receiving at doors 1 to 4, no put-away, replenishment, picking, packing or loading at doors 5 to 8, and no returns intake. The dispatcher suspends all carrier bookings for the shutdown period.

12. The date and duration of the shutdown are set by the warehouse manager, who is present on site for the count. At cut-off the WMS is frozen, open tasks are closed or suspended, and every pallet, case and unit in Zones A to F is counted blind, location by location, with a second count for every discrepancy. No adjustment from the stocktake is posted without a second count.

13. Only the warehouse manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results and any adjustment arising from it. Sign-off is personal and in writing in the WMS and on the paper record with name, date and time. Harborwick will not post stocktake adjustments or lift the WMS freeze until that sign-off is given.

14. Harborwick retains the full audit trail for all counts: location, SKU, quantity before and after, first count, second count, third count where taken, reason, preparer and approver. Open variances, blocked bays including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, and pending approvals are reported to the client on request and at the next scheduled review.

title: 2.3 Operating Hours and Inventory Reporting
text:
1. Harborwick's standard operating hours are Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, aligned to the two rostered shifts. All warehouse activity in Zones A to F and all dock activity at doors 1 to 8 takes place within these windows.

2. The morning shift runs 06:00 to 14:00. The afternoon shift runs 14:00 to 22:00, providing continuous cover Monday to Friday. Handover between supervisors takes place at 14:00 under PR-15, and the site is closed at 22:00 with overnight status recorded for the next morning shift at 06:00.

3. One shift supervisor is in charge of the floor on every shift. Harborwick does not operate any shift, receiving window or dispatch window without its supervisor present on site and contactable for the full period, including breaks.

4. Client order cut-offs, carrier time slots and replenishment and picking waves are planned within the standard windows. No picking, put-away to Zone B, E or F, packing, loading or returns intake is scheduled outside 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 without an approved overtime arrangement.

5. No routine weekend working is included in the service. Saturday and Sunday are non-working days, except for Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, limited to the morning period. No Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday operation is offered.

6. Overtime is approved only by the warehouse manager. No other role extends a shift, calls staff in for Saturday morning work or changes the standard pattern of 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. Approval is personal, in advance where possible, and covers the date, period, roles required and reason.

7. Every overtime approval is recorded with date, time and staffing, and is communicated to the client and carriers where it affects receiving or dispatch capacity. The shift supervisor confirms sufficient supervision, dock and zone cover before overtime work begins.

8. Harborwick commits that the WMS is the sole system of record for inventory and operations reporting. Stock in the system is stock on the rack after document check in Zone A, scan verification in Zone C, and WMS booking with scannable pallet licence plate. No hand-written or off-system quantity is reported as available.

9. Harborwick provides a daily inventory position on every working day by close of the afternoon shift. The report shows closing balance by SKU, batch and expiry where applicable, location by zone, inbound receipts booked in the period, outbound loads dispatched from Zone D, and quantities in quarantine in Zone F and in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage against the 4,000 kg limit.

10. Cycle count activity is reported weekly. The report summarises locations counted across Zones A to F on the rotating schedule, matches, variances confirmed by second count, adjustments posted with shift supervisor approval, and open variances, blocked bays including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, and pending approvals.

11. No adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08. Adjustments arising from daily cycle counts are approved only by the shift supervisor; adjustments arising from the annual wall-to-wall stocktake are approved only by the warehouse manager. The audit trail of first count, second count, third count where taken, reason, preparer and approver is retained and available to the client on request.

12. Harborwick carries out a full wall-to-wall stocktake once per calendar year with the site shut down and the WMS frozen at cut-off. The date and duration are set by the warehouse manager and notified to clients and carriers in advance. Only the warehouse manager signs off the results and any adjustment arising from it, and Harborwick issues the signed stocktake summary by zone, SKU and value after sign-off.

13. Operational exceptions are reported daily. The report includes shortages and overages at receiving in Zone A, quarantine moves to Zone F the same day they are found, scan-verification failures and short picks in Zone C, and any door, leveller or scanner fault affecting bookings or releases, with dispatcher and shift supervisor references.

14. Continuity between shifts is ensured under PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00, covering dock status at doors 1 to 8, vehicles in the marked waiting area, open WMS tasks for the 20 scanners, staged loads in Zone D, manual temperature verification in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, and quarantine and hazmat quantities in Zone F.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
text:
1. Harborwick handles all damaged, leaking, wet, open, collapsed or suspect goods under PR-09. Any such goods found in Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone or Zone F itself are moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day they are found. No damaged stock remains in its original zone overnight.

2. Quarantine is located in Zone F within the 600 m² services and control area. It is a physically separated, barriered and clearly signed area, distinct from packing, returns inspection and the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage. Harborwick keeps quarantine lanes clear and available at all times.

3. Harborwick commits to the same-day quarantine standard for every client. On finding damage the floor staff secure the area, report immediately to the shift supervisor and transfer the pallet to Zone F only on supervisor direction. No sorting, re-stacking or disposal takes place at the original location.

4. Transfer to quarantine is booked in the WMS to quarantine status before the pallet leaves its zone. Harborwick records date, zone and location found, SKU, batch and expiry where applicable, quantity, pallet identity, nature of damage and finder name, and applies a quarantine label. Goods booked to quarantine status are not available for replenishment, picking or dispatch.

5. Goods in quarantine remain physically separated and clearly identified by quarantine label and WMS status until formally released or written off. Harborwick will not pick, pack or load any quarantined pallet for any client order.

6. Damaged goods from receiving inspection in Zone A are not counted as available stock. Harborwick segregates them in Zone A, books them to quarantine status only and moves them to Zone F the same day, recording the quantity, damage type and pallet reference for write-off approval.

7. Damaged bulk or pick-face stock found during storage in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C or dispatch staging in Zone D is removed from its location immediately. Harborwick leaves the affected bay, face or lane empty and blocks it in the WMS where applicable until cleared.

8. Damaged hazardous materials are quarantined the same day under PR-09 and PR-13 and stored only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. Harborwick counts the quantity against the cage limit of 4,000 kg at all times, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, and never holds damaged hazmat outside the cage.

9. Damaged chilled goods from Zone E are segregated in place, booked to quarantine status where required and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day. Harborwick does not return them to Zone E and does not pick, pack or load them pending disposition.

10. Harborwick applies fixed write-off approval thresholds for every client. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR. Thresholds are not aggregated or split to avoid escalation and approvals are not delegable.

11. Approval is personal and recorded in the WMS and on the quarantine record with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and quarantine reference. Harborwick will not action a write-off, scrap or disposal without both entries completed.

12. No inventory adjustment for quarantine, scrap or restock is posted without a second count under PR-08. Where a write-off quantity is disputed, Harborwick will carry out the second count via the stock controller and record the result before approval is given.

13. Harborwick notifies the client of each quarantine event on the daily exceptions report, with date, location, SKU, quantity, reason and WMS quarantine reference, and provides photographs where racking, pallet or product damage is involved. Open quarantine quantities, pending approvals and blocked bays, including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, are included in the weekly inventory report until cleared.

14. Scrapped quantities remain in quarantine, clearly marked as scrap and segregated by product type, pending collection for disposal. Harborwick does not return scrapped food, drugstore or hazmat quantities to Zone C or Zone D and retains the full audit trail of quarantine moves, second counts and threshold approvals for client review.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.2 Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick handles all returns under PR-07 in Zone F within the 600 m² services and control area. All returned goods are received, recorded and inspected only in the returns inspection area in Zone F. No returns are inspected, stored or dispositioned in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E, and no returns are handled at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 calendar days of the original delivery date only. The delivery date is taken from the outbound manifest and proof of delivery for that load, counted as calendar days from delivery to presentation at site. Returns presented after 14 days are not accepted.

3. All returns arrive by prior booking at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4 at a time slot agreed with the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns door and slot before arrival. Carriers report to the gate or dispatcher and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the fenced yard.

4. Before unloading Harborwick checks returns paperwork in Zone A: customer name, original order and outbound load reference, delivery date, SKU and quantity presented, and reason for return. The 14-day eligibility and door and slot assignment are verified at that point.

5. Where the delivery was more than 14 days ago, the customer or order cannot be matched, or the quantity would breach the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load or the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F, Harborwick will refuse the return at the door. Refusal is recorded with date, time, door, carrier and reason and countersigned by the shift supervisor.

6. Accepted returns are moved directly to Zone F and booked in the WMS to returns status on arrival, with customer, original order, delivery date, return date, SKU, quantity, pallet identity and reason. They are physically separated, clearly signed as returns and are not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

7. Harborwick commits to unit-by-unit inspection of every returned item in Zone F. Inspection is carried out by the returns and packing staff under PR-07 against a bench checklist: outer packaging, inner seal integrity, labelling and batch or expiry, leakage, wetting, contamination, odour, temperature condition for chilled goods, and evidence of use or tampering.

8. Inspection is recorded with inspector name, date and time per pallet or unit in the WMS. No bulk acceptance or sample check replaces individual inspection. Goods remain in returns status in Zone F until inspection and proposal are complete.

9. Any goods found damaged, leaking, wet, open, out-of-temperature or suspect during returns inspection are segregated immediately. Harborwick books them to quarantine status in the WMS, labels them as quarantine and moves them to the physically separated quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

10. Hazardous materials presented as returns are handled only under PR-13. They are stored only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, subject at all times to the 4,000 kg cage limit, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, with incompatible classes segregated as marked.

11. On completion of inspection Harborwick proposes disposition for each inspected quantity in the WMS as restock, rework or scrap, with condition, quantity for each route and reason. No returned goods are restocked, reworked or scrapped without that proposal entered.

12. Final disposition of all inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor before any move from Zone F. Restock is approved only where goods are intact, sealed, correctly labelled and within expiry and cold-chain; rework remains in the value-added packing area in Zone F until reinspected and re-approved; scrap is booked to scrap and held in quarantine pending disposal.

13. No inventory adjustment for restock, rework or scrap is posted without a second count under PR-08. Where a quantity is disputed, Harborwick will carry out the second count via the stock controller and record the result before approval. Write-off thresholds for damaged quantities apply as per PR-09.

14. Harborwick retains the full audit trail for each return: eligibility check, receipt to returns status, inspection record, quarantine transfer where applicable, proposed disposition and supervisor approval with name, date and WMS reference. The client is notified of acceptance, refusal, inspection outcome and final disposition on the daily exceptions report.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA
text:
1. Harborwick provides temperature-controlled storage only in Zone E within the 6,000 m² hall. Zone E is a physically segregated, insulated enclosure of 300 m² with self-closing doors, held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12. No chilled storage is offered in any other zone.

2. Harborwick commits to maintain Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times while goods are stored. The commitment applies to standard operating hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday and to any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager.

3. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +8 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced, reset or ignored without investigation by the shift supervisor.

4. In addition to continuous monitoring, Harborwick carries out a manual temperature verification in Zone E on every shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, and during any approved Saturday morning overtime. The check is performed on a calibrated thermometer and recorded with date, time, measured temperature, operator name and signature, and countersigned by the shift supervisor. The log is retained in Zone E.

5. Only goods identified by the client as requiring chilled storage and booked with cold-chain status are stored in Zone E. Harborwick will check temperature condition and expiry where applicable during inspection in Zone A before booking. Goods not booked as chilled will not be placed in Zone E.

6. Put-away to Zone E is released only from Zone A after count, inspection and WMS booking with cold-chain status. Pallets for Zone E are moved directly to a directed vacant chilled location. Harborwick does not stage chilled pallets in ambient Zones A, B, C or D.

7. Goods in Zone E remain on pallets, stable, wrapped and within the pallet footprint under the site limit of 1,000 kg per pallet including load. No pallet is placed in doorways, against evaporators, across aisles or outside marked chilled positions. Doors to Zone E remain closed except during active put-away, replenishment or count.

8. Access to Zone E is restricted to authorised operators acting on a released WMS task and to the shift supervisor. Exposure time is minimised; personnel and electric pallet jacks rated for chilled operation enter only to complete the task and then exit.

9. Harborwick commits to immediate cold-chain response. Any alarm, excursion outside +2 °C to +8 °C, door fault, icing, condensation, leakage or evidence of breach is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, who secures stock in place, closes doors and prevents any picking in Zone C, packing or dispatch of affected pallets.

10. Affected pallets are segregated in place, identified with quarantine labels and, where required, booked to quarantine status in the WMS. Harborwick moves suspect chilled goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. No affected pallet is restored to available stock, replenished or loaded without clearance.

11. No new put-away to Zone E takes place during an active alarm or verified excursion. Harborwick will not accept new chilled receipts into Zone E until temperature is verified stable between +2 °C and +8 °C and any defect to refrigeration, doors, monitoring or alarms is inspected and logged by the maintenance technician.

12. The maintenance technician maintains the refrigeration plant, doors, seals, monitoring and alarm system for Zone E and logs every inspection and repair. Any defect affecting temperature holding or alarms is escalated to the warehouse manager, and Zone E is not returned to normal use for new put-away until cleared by the manager.

13. Harborwick notifies the client of any excursion, alarm or quarantine transfer affecting the client's goods on the daily exceptions report, with date, time, zone, SKU, quantity, measured temperature and WMS quarantine reference. Open excursions, quarantined chilled quantities and pending clearances are included in the weekly inventory report until closed.

14. All manual verification records, continuous monitoring logs, alarm and incident reports, quarantine moves and clearances are retained as the cold-chain audit trail and made available to the client on request. Open Zone E actions, monitoring status and verification results are included in PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.
